## ADR-026: Delivery-side reconciliation (ORD-10) — `NeedsReview` state for ambiguous Gamevion order-creation failures (built 2026-08-14)

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-14, grilled with the founder one decision at a time via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, before any code touched.

**Context:** A fresh full-system audit (same session, see `prd.md` §14) re-confirmed ORD-10 (delivery-side reconciliation) as the one still-open item from `foundation-security.md` §3's split payment-side/delivery-side outcome — payment-side has had automatic stuck-order detection since ADR-021 (`app:reconcile-pending-payments`); delivery-side never got its counterpart. Investigating *why* surfaced it is structurally harder than payment-side, not merely unbuilt out of neglect:

Two genuinely distinct ambiguous-failure shapes exist in `OrderFulfillmentService`/`FulfillOrderJob`/`GamevionAdapter`, neither previously documented as two separate problems:

- **Gap X — silent stuck-`processing`.** A connection-level failure exhausts both the HTTP-layer retry (`TransientFailureRetryPolicy`, 3×/200-500-1000ms) and the job-level retry (`FulfillOrderJob`, 3×/10-30-60s backoff, per its own doc comment). The job lands in `failed_jobs`; the `Order` stays at `delivery_status=processing` forever, with **zero `supplier_response` recorded** — completely invisible in the Admin Panel today, only discoverable by querying `failed_jobs` directly.
- **Gap Y — unactioned `duplicate_reference`.** Gamevion's `/api/order` is idempotent on `referenceNumber` (confirmed live 2026-07-29, ADR-006's addendum) — a resubmit against an already-accepted reference returns `409`, which `GamevionAdapter::createOrder()` already normalizes to `supplier_response.error_code='duplicate_reference'`. This is **already recorded in the data today**, both going forward and retroactively for any past order that hit it — grep confirmed nothing in `app/` ever reads or acts on that specific value; it's treated identically to any other business-level delivery failure.

Unlike payment-side's `ReconcilePendingPaymentsCommand`, which can always resolve ambiguity by polling `PaymentGateway::getPayment()` keyed on `payment_ref` (guaranteed present before the gateway call ever happens), Gamevion's `checkStatus()` requires **its own invoice number** (`supplier_ref`) — confirmed via `GamevionAdapterTest`'s own doc comment ("Gamevion's OWN order id... never our reference_number") — and that invoice number is precisely the value missing in both Gap X and Gap Y. Re-confirmed live during this grilling session: Gamevion's entire API surface is 4 endpoints total (re-checked against `docs.gamevion.com/gamevion-api`, matching ADR-006's 2026-07-25 addendum; a live re-fetch attempt this session was blocked by the site returning `403` to automated fetches, so this rests on the last-confirmed record, flagged below to re-verify before shipping), none of which accept our `reference_number` as a lookup key; the `409` error body itself carries no invoice field either (status+description only, per `GamevionAdapter::failureFrom()`'s own doc comment). The founder additionally checked Gamevion's real merchant dashboard live during this session (screenshot reviewed together) — it supports Status/Payment Status/date-range filters and a "Search Invoice" field keyed on *Gamevion's own* invoice format, with **no reference-number search at all**. So automated resolution of Gap Y is not possible against Gamevion's currently-confirmed API or dashboard surface — only a human, manually cross-referencing the dashboard's date-range filter against the TARGET (player ID) and SERVICE (game) columns, can determine the real outcome.

This "safe to retry `createOrder()` by reusing `reference_number`, and `409` specifically means idempotent-duplicate" mechanism is confirmed specific to `GamevionAdapter`'s own implementation — the generic `SupplierAdapter` interface declares no idempotency contract at all. Per ADR-006's own standing principle ("never assume a supplier's auth scheme, response envelope, or validation-endpoint availability is uniform with any other supplier"), this design's auto-retry step (decision 3) must be **re-verified, not assumed**, if/when a second real supplier adapter is ever added — deliberately not generalized into a capability flag now, since only one supplier exists today (AGENTS.md's own "don't design for hypothetical future requirements").

**Decision:**

1. **Scope: Gap X and Gap Y only.** Orders stuck at `delivery_status=not_started` (the queue worker never picked up the job at all) are explicitly **out of scope** — a different root cause (infra/ops; already has its own documented gotcha in `AGENTS.md`), not a Gamevion-response ambiguity. Belongs to a future alerting/health-check concern, not this feature.

2. **New `DeliveryStatus` enum case: `NeedsReview`.** A typed state, not a flag/column layered on top of `Failed`/`Processing` — matches this project's own precedent (`PaymentStatus` gaining a typed field during the `ChipGateway` build, ADR-022's addendum) for the same reason: the type system forces every call site to handle it explicitly, rather than trust a convention a future change could silently miss.

3. **New scheduled command `app:reconcile-pending-deliveries`**, same 15-minute cadence as `app:reconcile-pending-payments` (`routes/console.php`). Targets orders stuck **>15 minutes** — comfortably past `FulfillOrderJob`'s own worst-case exhaustion window (up to ~9 attempts across HTTP + job-level retry layers):
   - **Gap X** (`supplier_ref` null, still `processing`): attempts **one** `createOrder()` retry, reusing the order's existing `reference_number` (ORD-8, never regenerated on retry). A real `invoice_number` back means it genuinely failed before and is now resolved — auto-mark `Delivered` exactly as a normal successful delivery would (credits ledger profit via the existing path). A `duplicate_reference` back falls through to `NeedsReview`, same as Gap Y.
   - **Gap Y** (`delivery_status=failed` with `error_code=duplicate_reference`, including any that already reached this state via a manual "Resend Delivery" click before this feature existed): moves directly to `NeedsReview` — no further automated resolution attempted, since neither Gamevion's API nor its dashboard support a reference-number lookup (confirmed above).

4. **`NeedsReview` has exactly three admin-facing exit actions:**
   a. **"Mark as Delivered"** (new action — no equivalent exists today, deliberately, since money-critical state has never trusted a bare admin claim before). Admin manually cross-references Gamevion's dashboard (date-range filter + TARGET/SERVICE columns — the only fields usable for this lookup, confirmed above) to determine the real outcome, then submits **with the real Gamevion invoice number they found** — this populates `supplier_ref` (closing the exact data gap that caused the ambiguity) and credits ledger profit through the same path a normal delivery does.
   b. **"Resend Delivery"** — the existing `OrderResendService`/modal, gate extended to also accept `delivery_status=NeedsReview` (currently `Failed`-only).
   c. **"Issue Voucher"** — **explicitly blocked** from `NeedsReview` (its existing gate stays `Failed`-only, deliberately not extended). This is the one exit this feature does not open, because voucher issuance from an unconfirmed state carries exactly the double-compensation risk (a customer receiving both real game credits Gamevion silently already delivered, and a store-credit refund) that this whole feature exists to prevent. An admin must resolve the order to `Delivered` or a genuine `Failed` first.

5. **Admin UI reuses the existing `/admin/orders` list + detail-view pattern** — a new filter value `needs_review` alongside the existing `need_action`/`processing`/`completed` filters, surfaced inside the existing Order detail view (no new standalone screen). For a `NeedsReview` order specifically, the detail view additionally surfaces `created_at`, `player_id`, and the game/service name prominently — exactly the fields needed to manually cross-reference Gamevion's dashboard.

6. **No backfill script.** The scheduled job scans by current state + elapsed time on every run, not by "when created" — any order already stuck in a Gap X or Gap Y state before this ships gets picked up automatically the first time the job runs post-deploy. No separate one-time migration/backfill needed.

**Rationale:** Gap X and Gap Y are handled by one job because they converge on the same terminal state and the same "no automated resolution possible" reality — splitting them into two features would duplicate the `NeedsReview` state, the admin UI, and the three exit actions for no real benefit. The one-retry-then-flag design (decision 3) mirrors this codebase's existing bias toward auto-resolving the common case (most connection blips are already healed by the two retry layers that ran *before* reaching this job; what's left after 15 minutes is disproportionately the genuinely-stuck minority) while refusing to guess on the genuinely ambiguous remainder. Decision 4c's asymmetry — two exits opened, one deliberately not — is the load-bearing decision of this whole ADR: every other choice here is either infrastructure (the job, the state) or a UI convenience; this is the one that actually prevents the double-compensation failure mode the founder specifically asked about being explicitly closed rather than left to admin discipline.

**Consequence to track:**
- This ADR records design intent only — no code exists yet, matching this project's own established practice for design-only ADRs (`ADR-013`/`ADR-015`/`ADR-016`/`ADR-017`/`ADR-018`/`ADR-020`/`ADR-022`/`ADR-024`/`ADR-025`). Update `docs/prd.md` §14/§15 once this actually ships.
- The "Gamevion has only 4 endpoints, no reference-number lookup anywhere" fact this whole design leans on is a **3-week-old record** (last confirmed live 2026-07-25) plus a founder-reviewed dashboard screenshot from this session — a live re-fetch attempt this session was blocked (`403`). Worth one more direct check with Gamevion support before shipping decision 4a's "no automated path exists" as a permanent fact, not just at design time.
- `createOrder()`'s idempotent-retry-by-`referenceNumber` semantics (decision 3) are a **Gamevion-specific** confirmed behavior, not a `SupplierAdapter` interface guarantee — flagged in Context above, re-verify explicitly before extending this auto-retry pattern to any future second supplier adapter.
- `NeedsReview`'s real-world trigger rate is genuinely unmeasured — this project has no live production traffic yet. The founder specifically asked about volume/burst risk (2,000 concurrent orders); the honest answer given was structural reasoning, not a real percentage. Worth watching the actual rate once live and revisiting the 15-minute threshold/job cadence if it turns out materially different from the "small tail, not a flood" expectation this design assumes.
- Every existing `match`/`switch` over `DeliveryStatus` (`OrderController`'s status filters, `OrderStatusService`'s transition guards, any frontend `DeliveryStatus` display mapping) needs an explicit audit at build time to confirm none of them silently mishandle the new `NeedsReview` case via a default/fallthrough branch — PHP's `match` (no fallthrough, throws on unmatched) mostly protects backend call sites structurally; TypeScript's own exhaustiveness needs the same check on the frontend.
- `OrderStatusService::startDelivery()`'s existing guard (`in_array($currentDeliveryStatus, [NotStarted, Failed])`) needs `NeedsReview` added so "Resend Delivery" (decision 4b) can actually re-enter `Processing` from that state.

**Addendum, 2026-08-14 (same session, after build) — sandbox coverage.** Founder asked whether `NeedsReview` could be exercised in the ADR-018 sandbox the same way a real order would hit it. Turned out to be nearly free: `ResendSandboxOrderDeliveryRequest`'s `error_code` field is already free-text, and `SandboxOrderController::resend()` already calls the exact same `OrderFulfillmentService::fulfill()` this ADR's duplicate_reference handling lives in — so typing `duplicate_reference` into the sandbox's existing "Simulated Outcome" picker reaches `needs_review` with zero backend changes. What *was* missing, both fixed same session: `SandboxOrderController` gained a `markDelivered()` counterpart to decision 4a (reusing `markDeliveredManually()` unchanged — `creditProfit()`'s existing `is_test` guard, decision #6 of ADR-018, already keeps this off the real ledger with no new guard needed), and `/middleware/sandbox`'s own Resend button was gated `=== "failed"` only, same oversight the real `/admin/orders` page had before this ADR's decision 4b fix — extended to match. 7 new backend tests, full suite **598/598 green**.

## ADR-027: VIP Membership — Costco-style spend-quota subscription, phone+OTP lightweight identity, member pricing (design only, not yet built)

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-21, grilled with the founder one decision at a time via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, before any code touched. **Founder's own explicit condition on recording this as "Accepted": every decision below stays open to being re-challenged in full at actual build time, not just refined** — he doesn't yet know when that will be, and by then real numbers (see Context) may exist that don't today. See Consequence to track.

**Context:** The founder brought a reference document from a separate discussion (with Gemini) proposing a subscription-based VIP membership tier for the topup store, modeled on Costco's wholesale-membership business (most operating profit from membership fees, not markup on goods sold — members buy near cost price, non-members pay full retail). Explicitly treated as external inspiration only, not ground truth for this project, per the founder's own framing at the start of the session.

This reference's own supporting numbers (22,181 completed & delivered orders, 6,105 unique customers, ~12.3% average gross margin, a 6-tier customer spend-distribution table) were initially assumed to come from a different, larger business — "kedairuncitsoloz," a real prospective partner whose real monthly sales the founder states range RM400k–2,000,000, roughly 3-15x this project's own real monthly revenue (RM66.5k–244k per `ADR-020`'s addendum). That partnership is not yet confirmed and kedairuncitsoloz's own real order/margin data is not yet available.

Mid-session, a real cross-check reversed that assumption: this project's own real order export (`/Users/farresyh/Downloads/orders.csv`, 28,848 rows — the exact same file already used for `ADR-020`'s capacity analysis, confirmed real, not the deleted `docs/orders.csv` copy) produced a paid+delivered order count (22,297) and spend-tier distribution (Micro 27.1%/Casual 29.8%/Regular 16.6%/Active 13.3%/Hardcore 9.7%/Whale 3.5%) matching the reference document's own numbers (22,181; 26.8%/29.7%/16.6%/13.6%/9.7%/3.6%) to within rounding. This is almost certainly the same underlying dataset, analyzed once by Gemini and once fresh in this session — meaning the reference's numbers describe **this project's own real history (under its `karrashop`/`keroxshop` branding), not kedairuncitsoloz's**. Kedairuncitsoloz's real numbers remain genuinely unknown. For this ADR, this project's own verified real order history is used as the reference dataset, with customer/order **counts** (not per-order unit economics) scaled ×5–×10 to approximate kedairuncitsoloz's stated volume range — the founder's own proposed approximation once the mistaken assumption above was surfaced.

The real analysis also corrected two numbers the reference and this project's own config had wrong: real weighted-average margin across the verified dataset is **5.59%** (`Σmarkup/Σcost`), well below both the reference's assumed 12.3% and this project's own `packages.default_markup_percent` config default of 15% (likely skewed low by "Weekly Diamond Pass" items dominating the sample — flagged to re-segment by package category before finalizing pricing, see Consequence). A live competitor price-check the same session found Malaysia's mainstream top-up resellers (Codashop, SEAGM, Joytify) cluster tightly around RM0.075–0.078/diamond for Mobile Legends, while a smaller, lesser-known site (gamejus.com) undercuts them at ~RM0.069/diamond — and this project's own real Gamevion cost for the same denomination (`Package` id 3, "13+1 Diamonds": `cost_price` RM0.94 against gamejus's real sale price RM0.96) is already almost at gamejus's own retail price, meaning beating gamejus specifically requires a member markup near 2%, not the 5–8% that would beat only the mainstream three.

This ADR also narrows `ADR-011` (storefront stays guest-checkout, no Customer account) rather than reversing it outright — see Decision 2/3.

**Decision:**

1. **Dual goal, not single**: both recurring subscription revenue and retention/lock-in are explicit objectives — the founder rejected treating "does the fee cover the margin given up" as the only lever worth optimizing, which is why Decision 8's breakeven check exists as a real constraint check, not the design's starting premise.

2. **Identity: phone number + OTP, not a full email/password Customer account.** A deliberately narrower reversal of `ADR-011` than the reference's own account-based model — the founder chose this specifically after confirming a member dashboard (status, quota, order history) is achievable without full account/session infrastructure. Verification and reminders both go over **WhatsApp** (Decision 11's billing channel and this identity channel share one vendor, not two).

3. **Profile materializes on demand, not universally.** Guest checkout's existing mandatory `customer_name`/`customer_email`/`customer_phone` fields (`CreateCheckoutRequest`) are unchanged — no new field, no new forced step for the ~87%+ of customers who won't subscribe. A phone-verified session is created only when a customer actively chooses to verify (to subscribe, or to check existing membership/order status). Because `Order.customer_phone` already exists as a plain column on every order, past and future orders link to a verified session by matching on phone — no new linkage table or Order schema change needed for order-history display.

4. **Two tiers, launched together, deliberate decoy/anchor pricing** — the founder's own framing, borrowed from cinema ticket-size pricing (Medium priced disproportionately close to Large, to nudge the upsell). Requires both tiers live simultaneously to work; a single-tier pilot would remove the anchor the psychology depends on. `membership_plans` must be a config-driven table (fee, quota, per row), not hardcoded tiers, so a future third tier is a data row, not a code change.

5. **Member price = the package's own configured `markup_percent`, reduced by a relative discount, floored at 0%** — never a flat member-wide markup override, and never sold below cost. Preserves this codebase's existing per-package markup customization (`Package.markup_percent`, admin-adjustable) instead of collapsing every package to one number regardless of its own real margin.

6. **Competitive target: beat the single cheapest verified competitor (gamejus.com), not just the mainstream cluster.** The founder's explicit, informed choice after seeing Decision 8's breakeven numbers — a materially thinner, higher-conviction margin than "just beat Codashop/SEAGM/Joytify" would have required.

7. **Quota is tracked and consumed in member-price-paid currency (RM actually charged at member rate), not cost price or a separately-computed retail-equivalent.** Avoids dual-accounting; matches the "RM100/RM200 spend cap" framing the founder used throughout. Resets on a **rolling 30-day cycle anchored to each member's own subscription date** — not a shared calendar-month reset — per the founder's own "standard business practice" framing (fairness for mid-month subscribers). Implementation note: this requires a daily scan for per-user cycle-elapsed rather than one shared cron trigger.

8. **Breakeven check against real data (this session), draft anchors only:** at the Decision 6 target (~2% member markup), forgone margin per RM100/150/200/300/500 of quota consumed is RM3.34/RM5.01/RM6.68/RM10.02/RM16.70 per month. The reference's own suggested fees (RM8.90, RM19.90) exceed forgone margin at every quota level tested, even at this aggressive target — informed the founder's Decision 6 choice. Draft shape floated for future discussion, **explicitly not final** (Consequence): Tier 1 ~RM8.90/mo at ~RM100 quota, Tier 2 ~RM19.90/mo at ~RM300 quota (not the reference's own RM500 — leaves headroom against the RM19.90 breakeven while widening the Decision 4 anchor gap).

9. **No cost price ever surfaces to the customer.** Product/browse pages show the normal price and a generic, non-personalized member price side by side, plus a "Save X%" badge computed as `(normal − member) / normal` — identical content for every visitor, cacheable, no per-visit DB lookup. Rejected the founder's own alternate idea (computing the shown discount off cost price directly) as unnecessarily convoluted for no real benefit over the simple normal-vs-member delta.

10. **Personalization happens once, at "Proceed to Pay," never at browse time.** A session-recognized existing member gets the member price silently; anyone else sees an optional, non-blocking prompt ("Verify & get member price" vs. "Continue as guest") — guest checkout is never gated or interrupted, preserving `ADR-011`'s original intent for every customer who doesn't opt in. This keeps the one DB-side membership/quota check to a single point per checkout, the same shape as this codebase's existing per-checkout checks (blacklist velocity guard, voucher validation, player-ID validation) — not a new class of load, and negligible against `ADR-020`'s own real burst numbers (busiest 5-minute window ever recorded: 28 orders).

11. **Billing: hybrid, gateway-dependent.** Manual renewal (a one-time payment link through the existing checkout/payment-gateway flow, no stored card) is the baseline, always available regardless of gateway. True recurring auto-charge is layered on only where the resolved gateway genuinely supports it — confirmed this session that Malaysia recurring billing is real but uneven across the project's two gateways: Xendit has a real Subscriptions API, but Malaysia-specific FPX/direct-debit self-serve activation isn't confirmed in its docs (activation contacts listed only for Indonesia/Philippines); CHIP's recurring is card-only via a saved token with no built-in scheduler, and has no FPX/e-wallet recurring at all. No commitment here to which gateway carries recurring for which channel — decide at build time against each gateway's then-current real capability, not this session's snapshot.

12. **Anti-abuse: the quota cap alone, for the pilot — no additional per-day/per-order rate limit.** The founder's own quota design (a hard monthly spend cap) is treated as sufficient first-line defense against the resale-arbitrage risk a near-cost member price creates on a liquid, resellable digital good; an additional rate limit is deliberately not built pre-emptively, matching this codebase's own established norm (`AGENTS.md`) against designing for a problem not yet observed. Revisit only if real abuse is seen.

13. **Member dashboard scope (the "what does a normal member get" the founder asked to pin down as step one)**: membership status + expiry + a renew action, remaining quota this cycle, and order history. The last is free from Decision 3's existing `Order.customer_phone` match — no new table needed to support it.

**Rationale:** Every layer of this design was kept deliberately smaller than the reference document's own version of it — identity is OTP-only, not full accounts; personalization is checkout-time-only, not page-load-time; quota consumption is designed to reuse this codebase's own proven concurrency-safe pattern (`LedgerService`/`VoucherService`'s row-locking, not a new mechanism — see Consequence); and Decision 6's aggressive margin target was only accepted after Decision 8's real breakeven math, not on the reference document's own optimism. The one deliberate exception to "keep it small" is Decision 4's two-simultaneous-tiers requirement — accepted specifically because the anchor/decoy psychology the founder wants structurally requires the comparison to exist from day one; a staged single-tier launch would remove the mechanism the founder is actually trying to use.

**Consequence to track:**
- This ADR records design intent only — no code exists yet, matching this project's own established practice for design-only ADRs (`ADR-013`/`ADR-015`/`ADR-016`/`ADR-017`/`ADR-018`/`ADR-020`/`ADR-022`/`ADR-024`/`ADR-025`/`ADR-026`). Update `docs/prd.md` §14/§15 once this actually ships.
- **Load-bearing founder instruction for this whole ADR**: every decision above is explicitly open to being re-argued from scratch at actual build time, not just tuned — he does not know when that will be, and kedairuncitsoloz's real order/margin data (if the partnership is confirmed by then) would be reason enough to revisit Decision 8's numbers specifically, and possibly others. Treat this ADR as the last-known-good starting point for that future conversation, not a locked spec.
- Decision 8's fee/quota numbers are draft anchors only — re-run the breakeven model against kedairuncitsoloz's real data once available, before finalizing anything.
- The 5.59% real weighted-average margin this ADR's breakeven math is built on is likely skewed low by "Weekly Diamond Pass" items dominating the sampled orders (thin-margin publisher-pass resales) — re-segment by package category before finalizing Decision 5/6/8's numbers at build time.
- Quota decrement (Decision 7) needs a race-safe implementation before shipping — reuse this codebase's existing row-lock concurrency pattern (`tests/Concurrency/LedgerWithdrawConcurrencyTest.php`, `VoucherRedeemConcurrencyTest.php`), don't design a new one.
- No OTP/WhatsApp-messaging vendor is integrated anywhere in this codebase today — Decision 2/11 settle the channel (WhatsApp) but not the vendor (Meta Cloud API vs. a BSP); a real new external dependency needs selecting and provisioning before build starts.
- Decision 6's aggressive gamejus-beating target assumes gamejus's own pricing stays where it was checked live this session (2026-08-21) — no competitor-price-drift monitoring is proposed here; re-verify before finalizing, not just at design time.
- The existing storefront backlog item (WhatsApp placeholder number, `OrderStatusTracker.tsx:151`/`BottomNav.tsx:17`, per `prd.md`'s live next-session pointer) should be resolved as part of standing up this feature's real WhatsApp number, not as a separate task — likely the same business number serves both.

## ADR-028: Platform & Reseller Settings — reseller-scoped branding vs. platform-wide config split (built 2026-08-22)

**Status:** Accepted — 2026-08-21 (grilled with the founder one decision at a time via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, before any code touched); **built and browser-verified 2026-08-22**, see its addendum below and `docs/prd.md` §14's matching entry

**Context:** Two live storefront backlog items — dead links in `SeoBlurb.tsx`/`SiteFooter.tsx` (real destination URLs never supplied) and a placeholder WhatsApp number in `OrderStatusTracker.tsx`/`BottomNav.tsx` plus a missing Terms & Conditions/Privacy Policy page — were sitting in `prd.md`'s standing pointer as "blocked on the founder." The founder pushed back on that framing: these values are hardcoded directly in storefront component code today because no admin-editable settings mechanism exists at all (`prd.md` §6.17 SET-1..11 / §6.16 SEO-1..7 are ✅ tracked MVP-priority requirements, currently 100% ⬜ not started per §15) — not because the founder is withholding the actual values. Building the settings mechanism turns "blocked on a dev session every time a link changes" into "founder edits it in the admin panel," which is the real fix; the two backlog items are downstream symptoms, not the thing to solve directly.

`Reseller` (`ADR-013`: the platform owner is the first row, not a parallel single-tenant concept) has no branding/contact/SEO fields today — only business/pricing columns (`business_name`, `contact_name`, `email`, `phone`, `markup_pct`, `max_markup_pct`, `domains`, `status`, `xendit_subaccount_id`, `notes`). `prd.md` §6.17 describes SET-1/SET-5/SET-10 as flat "Admin Settings" with no reconciliation against the `Reseller` table's existence, and multi-reseller domain-routing is itself still an open question (§12: "Will reseller domains (Phase 2) use subdomains or custom domains... needs a design pass before Phase 2 starts") — so today's storefront is a single deployment serving exactly one `Reseller` row, resolved via the existing `Reseller::platformOwner()` helper (already used by `CheckoutController`/`CatalogController`).

**Decision:**

1. **Split SET-1..11 into two homes by nature, not by numbering: `reseller_branding` (per-reseller, customer-facing) and `platform_settings` (global singleton, ops-facing).** Grouping by "does a future second reseller need their own copy of this, or is it inherently one-per-deployment" cleanly separates every item — see decisions 2/3 below for the actual split.

2. **`reseller_branding` — a new table, 1:1 with `Reseller` (`reseller_id` FK), not columns added directly onto `Reseller`.** Holds: store display name, description, support email, support phone/WhatsApp, Telegram contact link, footer content, social media links (JSON), Terms & Conditions content, Privacy Policy content (SET-1's customer-facing subset, SET-5, SET-10, plus the T&C/Privacy page content the missing-page backlog item needs). Kept as its own table rather than bloating `Reseller` with ~8-10 unrelated columns — mirrors this codebase's existing convention of splitting a distinct concern into its own table rather than growing an existing model (`deactivation_logs`/`price_change_logs` beside `packages`), and keeps `Reseller` itself focused on the business/pricing fields it already has. Deliberately built now, ahead of any real second reseller existing, because a future affiliate/reseller program is a real, stated direction (not a hypothetical) — the founder's own reasoning for accepting this shape over a simpler global-only table.

3. **`Reseller.email`/`Reseller.phone` and `reseller_branding`'s own support-contact fields are deliberately separate, not reused.** The former is internal (admin's own contact channel to reach that reseller); the latter is customer-facing (what a guest sees on the storefront). Conflating them would mean an admin editing their own internal contact record accidentally changes what customers see, or vice versa.

4. **`platform_settings` — a new table, singleton row (not a generic key-value `key`/`value`/`type` store).** Holds: currency, system-wide markup % (SET-2's "apply to all packages" bulk action — likely a default-for-new-packages value plus a triggered bulk-update, not just a stored number; exact mechanics left to the build session), maintenance mode flag + custom message (SET-6), Telegram bot integration (SET-9 — confirmed by the founder as an ops tool, admins receiving order notifications via Telegram, not a customer-facing reseller bot). Fixed columns, not key-value: matches this codebase's own established house style (money is always a typed `_sen` column, never a generic `value` field; every existing settings-shaped model — `Reseller`, `PaymentMethod` — uses fixed columns) and there is no existing precedent anywhere in this codebase for a generic settings-value pattern to extend instead.

5. **SET-4 (backup schedule/retention) excluded from this ADR's scope — genuinely blocked by deployment, not just unbuilt.** `prd.md` §12's own still-open question ("Will backups be stored on local server or cloud storage?") depends on `ADR-020`'s hosting decision, which isn't provisioned yet. A retention-period setting with no real backup job running anywhere to consume it would be inert — the founder's own bar from Q1 of this grilling session ("kalau perkara lain tu tak di block oleh deployment... worth buat") explicitly excludes this. Revisit once `ADR-020` provisioning happens.

6. **SET-8 (email notification toggles) and SET-9's actual sending mechanism excluded — no notification-sending infrastructure exists anywhere in this codebase today.** Confirmed by a direct grep, not assumed: zero `Mail::`/`Notification::` usage anywhere in `app/`; `AdminUser`'s `Notifiable` trait is unused default Laravel scaffolding. SET-9's own *setting* (a stored bot token/chat-id row) is kept in `platform_settings` per decision 4 above since it's cheap and the right home once built, but the feature that would actually consume it — a real notification-sending mechanism (provider choice, queue job, templates) — is a separate, unscoped piece of work, matching this codebase's own established principle against designing a setting for a mechanism that doesn't exist yet (the same reasoning as decision 5).

7. **SET-7 (payment gateway toggle) and SET-11 (transaction fee config) stay exactly where they already are — the Payment Methods tool (`/middleware/payment-methods`), a founder decision from 2026-07-25 predating this ADR — not folded into either new table.** SET-3 (reseller default/max markup, auto-approve) stays Phase 2, unchanged, no real second reseller to configure yet.

8. **Maintenance mode blocks new checkout submissions only — browsing, order tracking, and payment/webhook routes stay live.** A customer who already paid must still be able to check their order status during a maintenance window, and an in-flight payment's webhook must still be able to land and fulfil — freezing those would risk a paid, undelivered order with no way to recover it without manually flipping the flag back off first. Enforced at the specific write endpoint (`POST /api/checkout`), not a blanket route-group gate.

9. **`Reseller::platformOwner()` is reused for the new public branding endpoint, not a second lookup mechanism invented alongside it — with its own risk of being missed later written down twice, not once.** Same hardcoded-to-the-single-MVP-row pattern `CheckoutController`/`CatalogController` already use, and the same caveat `ADR-013` already recorded for those two call sites now explicitly extends to a third: `Reseller::platformOwner()`'s own doc comment gets updated to enumerate every call site once this is built, so a future session replacing it for real Phase 2 domain-routing has one place that lists everywhere it needs to change — not a call site quietly missed because the ADR that mentioned it wasn't re-read.

**Rationale:** The reseller-scoped/platform-wide split (decisions 1-4) isn't cosmetic — it's the same distinction `ADR-013` already drew for pricing/ledger (every Order references a `Reseller`, but ledger accounting itself is platform-wide infrastructure) applied to a new area, and building `reseller_branding` as its own table now means a real second reseller (Phase 2, or sooner if the affiliate/reseller direction the founder mentioned materializes) gets working branding for free, no later data migration out of a global-only settings table. Decisions 5/6 both trace back to one principle stated repeatedly elsewhere in this codebase's own history (`ADR-015`/`ADR-016`/`ADR-020` decision #1): don't design a setting for a mechanism that doesn't exist yet — a toggle with nothing behind it is worse than no toggle, since it implies a capability the platform doesn't actually have.

**Consequence to track:**
- ~~This ADR records design intent only — no code exists yet...~~ **Built and browser-verified, 2026-08-22 — see this ADR's addendum below and `docs/prd.md` §14's matching entry. `docs/prd.md` §15 updated accordingly.**
- ~~Decision 9's doc-comment update to `Reseller::platformOwner()` must actually happen as part of the build...~~ **Done, 2026-08-22 — the method's doc comment now lists every call site, including the two this build added (`BrandingController`, `Admin\SettingsController`).**
- `ADR-027`'s own Consequence to track already flags the WhatsApp-number backlog item as likely sharing a real business number with VIP Membership's planned OTP channel — once `reseller_branding`'s support-WhatsApp field is populated with a real number, cross-check against whichever number `ADR-027` eventually uses, don't let the two silently diverge.
- ~~SET-2's "apply to all packages" bulk markup action needs its own mechanics decision at build time...~~ **Decided and built, 2026-08-22 — a one-time bulk-update over existing active packages (not a stored default for new ones), mirroring `PackageController::updateMarkup()`'s own `PriceChangeLog` write. See `docs/prd.md` §14.**
- The T&C/Privacy Policy *content* itself (the actual legal text) remains blocked on the founder regardless of this ADR — building the field/page this ADR describes only changes where that content would live once supplied, it doesn't supply it.
- A companion ADR for SEO-1..7 (SEO Management) is the founder's own next step after this one, grilled separately — some of its decisions (whether `reseller_branding` also carries SEO defaults, whether per-game SEO's already-existing `Game.seo_*` columns need any schema change) will read on this ADR's table shape; sequence that grilling session after this one is at least drafted, not in parallel.

**Addendum, 2026-08-22 — Footer Settings split into its own tab/table, three new legal-page routes, rich text + templating for legal content, and a bounded Footer Games feature (grilled with the founder via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, mockup-driven — reviewing a working HTML skeleton of the Settings screen surfaced every decision below).**

**Context:** Reviewing a visual mockup of this ADR's Settings screen, the founder identified two real gaps decision 2 didn't anticipate: (a) footer content (footer text, legal-page text) is conceptually distinct from "branding" (store identity/contact info) and deserves its own tab/table rather than crowding Store Branding further, and (b) the missing-legal-page backlog item (`prd.md`'s standing pointer, items 1/2) needs an **About Us** page too, not just T&C/Privacy — `SiteFooter.tsx`'s "Company" column links to all three (`About Us`, `Terms & Conditions`, `Privacy Policy`), all three equally unlinked plain text today. Separately, the founder specified the legal content needs real rich-text formatting (a specific toolbar: bold/italic/underline/strikethrough/ordered+unordered list/link/clear-formatting) and a `{store_name}` template variable, so the same legal text template can be reused by a future second reseller (the affiliate/reseller direction decision 2 already anticipated) without manually rewriting the store name throughout the prose for each one.

**Decision:**

10. **Split decision 2's `reseller_branding` further: legal/footer content moves to a new `reseller_footer_settings` table (1:1 `Reseller`, same shape convention as `reseller_branding`), leaving `reseller_branding` holding only store identity/contact fields.** `reseller_branding` keeps: store name, description, support email/phone, WhatsApp, social links. `reseller_footer_settings` gains: `footer_text` (moved out of `reseller_branding`), `terms_content`, `privacy_content` (both moved — decision 2 originally put these in `reseller_branding`; this addendum relocates them), `about_us_content` (new — not in the original ADR). The Settings screen gains a third tab, **Footer Settings**, alongside Store Branding and Platform Settings.

11. **Three new storefront routes — `/terms`, `/privacy`, `/about-us` — render `reseller_footer_settings`'s three content fields.** None exist today (confirmed: zero files under `storefront/src` for any of the three; `SiteFooter.tsx`'s footer links for all three are plain unlinked `<li>` text). Closes the missing-legal-page half of `prd.md`'s standing pointer items 1/2 (the WhatsApp-number half is unaffected — still `reseller_branding`, per decision 2).

12. **Legal content is rich text (HTML), not plain text — stored sanitized, sanitized again at render (defense in depth).** Persisted format is HTML, not Markdown: the founder's required toolbar includes Underline, which CommonMark/GFM has no native syntax for — storing Markdown would still need raw `<u>` HTML passthrough, reopening the same sanitization problem while adding a conversion layer for no benefit. `league/commonmark` (an existing but *transitive*, not direct, dependency of `laravel/framework` — confirmed via `composer why`) is not relevant here; it converts Markdown → HTML and nothing in this feature stores Markdown. Sanitization uses a **new direct dependency, `mews/purifier`** (no HTML sanitizer/purifier exists anywhere in this codebase today — confirmed via `composer.json`) — chosen over hand-rolled `strip_tags()` because the allowlist includes `a[href]`, and `strip_tags()` only strips disallowed *tags*, not disallowed *attributes/schemes* (a `javascript:` href on an allowed `<a>` tag would survive it untouched). Allowlist: `b/strong, i/em, u, s/strike, ol, ul, li, a[href], p, br`.

13. **`{store_name}` is a template token, substituted at storefront render time only (not at admin save time), resolving to that reseller's own `reseller_branding.store_name`.** Render-time substitution (not save-time) means a future store-name change is reflected in legal pages automatically, without re-editing every legal field. The admin editor shows a live preview with the token already resolved, for proofreading, but the stored value keeps the raw `{store_name}` token. Any other brace sequence (a typo, an unrecognized token) is left verbatim — no error, no "did you mean" detection; `{store_name}` is the only recognized token today.

14. **Footer Games: admin picks up to 4 currently-active games, stored as an ordered list, to feature in the storefront footer's "Top Up Games" section.** Stored as an ordered JSON array of `game_id` on `reseller_footer_settings` (order = display order — footer position matters, same reasoning `hero_slides.sort_order` already established for an analogous "admin picks N items, order matters for display" case, confirmed as existing precedent). Only games with `Game.is_active = true` are selectable (no named `scopeActive` exists on `Game` today, unlike `HeroSlide::scopeLive()` — confirmed live; a build-time detail whether to add one). A reseller with fewer than 4 active games, or none picked yet, renders however many are actually picked (0–4); zero picked hides the entire "Top Up Games" footer block rather than showing an empty heading.

15. **`reseller_footer_settings` gets the same edit rigor as `reseller_branding` — a single-admin save, no maker-checker.** This is customer-facing copy/config, not money movement; no reason to hold it to `Withdrawals`/`Vouchers`-level review.

16. **Both new dependencies are built as reusable primitives from day one, not inlined into this one feature — justified by this feature's own 3x internal reuse (T&C/Privacy/About Us all need the same rich-text editing), not speculative future-proofing.** Frontend: one shared `<RichTextEditor>` component (`admin/src/components/ui/RichTextEditor.tsx`, wrapping `@tiptap/react` + `@tiptap/starter-kit` + `@tiptap/extension-underline` + `@tiptap/extension-link`) — any future admin-authored rich-text field (e.g. `ADR-027`'s VIP Membership terms) reuses this component rather than re-integrating Tiptap from scratch. Backend: one named `mews/purifier` config profile (`config/purifier.php`, key `rich_text`) holding this addendum's allowlist — a future feature needing the *same* allowlist reuses this profile; one needing a different allowlist adds a new named profile alongside it rather than loosening this one.

**Rationale:** Splitting footer/legal content out of `reseller_branding` (decision 10) follows the same "distinct concern gets its own table" convention decision 2 itself already used to justify `reseller_branding` as separate from `Reseller` — footer/legal content is a genuinely different editing surface (long-form formatted text vs. short identity fields) from store branding, and letting it crowd `reseller_branding` indefinitely would eventually force the same split later, with a real migration this time instead of a clean design-time decision. Decisions 12-13 (HTML storage, render-time templating) both trace back to reasoning already established elsewhere in this codebase: money is computed at the moment of use, not trusted from storage (`ORD-9`) — `{store_name}` follows the identical shape, resolved live rather than baked in, so the two systems (branding, legal content) can never silently drift out of sync.

**Consequence to track (addendum):**
- ~~This addendum is design-only, same as the ADR it amends — no code exists yet.~~ **Built and browser-verified, 2026-08-22 (same day) — see the entry appended to `docs/prd.md` §14.**
- `mews/purifier` is a new direct Composer dependency — the first sanitizer/purifier of any kind in this codebase. Worth a deliberate look at its own maintenance/audit status at build time, same "checked, not assumed" discipline this project applies to every new dependency (`ADR-029`'s own `@next/third-parties` research is the precedent).
- ~~Decision 14's Footer Games feature has no `Game.scopeActive` yet...~~ **Resolved, 2026-08-22 — built querying the raw `is_active` column directly (matching this codebase's existing `GameController` convention), no new scope added.**
- If a real second reseller is onboarded before a self-service reseller portal exists (Phase 2, RES-1..6), whoever configures that reseller's `reseller_footer_settings` needs to know the `{store_name}` convention exists — not otherwise discoverable from the schema alone. Worth a short doc comment on the column itself once built.

## ADR-029: SEO Management — reseller-scoped SEO settings, redirects, and per-game wiring (built 2026-08-22)

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-21 (grilled with the founder one decision at a time via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, companion to and sequenced immediately after `ADR-028`, before any code touched)

**Context:** `prd.md` §6.16 (SEO-1..7) is 100% ⬜ not started per §15, all MVP-priority except SEO-3/SEO-5 ("Important"). One piece already exists: `Game` (`app/Models/Game.php`) already carries `seo_title`/`seo_title_local`/`seo_description`/`seo_description_local`/`seo_keywords`/`seo_og_image` columns — schema-complete, but never wired into `EditGameModal` (§15's own "GAME-12/SEO fields still unbuilt" note). `ADR-028`'s own Consequence to track named two open questions for this ADR to resolve: whether `reseller_branding` also carries SEO defaults, and whether `Game.seo_*` needs any schema change.

**Decision:**

1. **Per-game SEO (SEO-4) stays exactly where it already is — `Game.seo_*` columns, wired into the existing `/admin/games` `EditGameModal` — not folded into any new reseller-scoped table.** This resolves `ADR-028`'s first open question: a product page's own SEO (a specific game's title/description/keywords) is about that *product*, not about which reseller happens to be selling it — a different axis entirely from SEO-2/3/5/6/7 below, which are about the *storefront itself*. Games are global per `ADR-013`'s own established model (no per-reseller `Game` rows), so per-game SEO staying global too is the consistent choice, not a new one.

2. **SEO-2/3/6/7 — new table `reseller_seo_settings`, 1:1 with `Reseller`, kept separate from `ADR-028`'s `reseller_branding` despite both being per-reseller.** Resolves `ADR-028`'s second open question: `reseller_branding` is "how the store presents itself to a human visitor" (name, contact, footer); this table is "how the store presents itself to a search engine or tracking script" — a genuinely different concern that happens to share the same 1:1-with-`Reseller` shape, matching this codebase's existing convention of a separate table per distinct concern rather than one growing model. Holds: default meta title/description/OG image (SEO-2, used as the storefront's fallback wherever a specific `Game.seo_*` field is empty); meta title/description template *patterns* per page type with placeholder substitution, e.g. `{game_name} Top Up — {store_name}` (SEO-3); typed pixel-ID columns `ga_measurement_id`, `fb_pixel_id`, `tiktok_pixel_id` (SEO-7); a generic `custom_head_script`/`custom_body_end_script` fallback pair for anything not covered by the three named integrations (SEO-6).

3. **Redirects (SEO-5) — new table `redirects`, reseller-scoped (`reseller_id` FK), `from_path`/`to_path`/`status_code` (301/302).** Consistent with every other table in this ADR and `ADR-028`: a redirect is a path on a specific storefront's URL space, and a Phase 2 reseller with their own domain would need their own redirect set, not a shared global one.

4. **SEO-1 (Overview dashboard) needs no new storage at all — a computed, read-only view aggregating existing data (`Game.seo_*` completeness, `redirects` count) into a coverage checklist, never a single weighted "score."** A bespoke scoring formula would be a vanity metric invented without real basis; a checklist ("12/20 games have an SEO title", "3 games missing an OG image") is directly actionable without needing one.

5. **Implementation approach — verified against this project's own installed Next.js 16 docs (`admin/node_modules/next/dist/docs/`), not assumed from training data, per `admin/AGENTS.md`'s own warning that this Next.js version can differ from training-data assumptions.** No SEO framework needed:
   - **Meta tags/OG (SEO-2/3/4):** Next.js App Router's native `generateMetadata()` — already sufficient; deliberately not adding `next-seo` (a Pages-Router-era package whose core purpose App Router's native API already covers, confirmed by reading the bundled docs directly rather than assumed).
   - **Google Analytics/Tag Manager (part of SEO-7):** `@next/third-parties/google`'s `<GoogleAnalytics gaId="G-XYZ">`/`<GoogleTagManager gtmId="GTM-XYZ">` components — an official Vercel-maintained package (confirmed present in this project's own bundled Next.js docs), not currently installed, a genuine new dependency worth adding rather than hand-rolling Google's own script-loading optimizations.
   - **Facebook Pixel/TikTok Pixel + the SEO-6 custom-script fallback:** `next/script` — already built into Next.js core, zero new dependency, no official or compelling third-party package exists for either platform since they're just a standard init snippet with a dynamic ID, which `next/script`'s own loading-strategy options already handle correctly.
   - **Redirects (SEO-5) execution:** a custom lookup against the `redirects` table (via `proxy.ts`/middleware or an equivalent storefront-side check) — no existing package fits a schema-specific, admin-editable, per-reseller redirect set; this is genuinely bespoke, not reinventing something that already exists.

6. **Access model: the Admin Panel edits these settings on behalf of a reseller — today always `Reseller::platformOwner()` — there is no reseller self-service portal (RES-1..6, Phase 2, not built).** Both this ADR's tables and `ADR-028`'s carry a `reseller_id` FK so the data model is ready, but the *editor* today is exactly the same admin who already manages Games/Packages/Vouchers for the whole platform, not a distinct reseller identity. Mirrors `ADR-013`'s own "same code path, more rows" philosophy: when Phase 2 eventually builds a real reseller self-service portal, it reuses these same tables and endpoints, scoped to the logged-in reseller's own `reseller_id` instead of full admin access — no schema change needed at that point, only a new UI surface and an auth-scoping layer.

7. **Sequencing: design-only, same as `ADR-028` — building either ADR is a future session's work, one item at a time, not authorized to start from this grilling session alone.**

**Rationale:** The one real insight this session turned up is decision 1's axis distinction — per-game SEO and per-storefront SEO look similar (both are "SEO settings") but vary along completely different dimensions (which product vs. which reseller), and conflating them into one table would have been the wrong shape the moment a second reseller or a second game both needed SEO data simultaneously. Decision 5's research (reading this project's own bundled Next.js docs rather than assuming) closes out a real, previously-open question — the founder asked directly whether an existing library could help — with a concrete, low-dependency answer: exactly one new package (`@next/third-parties`, official) is worth adding, everything else is already native to the Next.js version this project runs.

**Consequence to track:**

- ~~`@next/third-parties` is explicitly **experimental**...~~ **Re-verified 2026-08-22 immediately before installing — still explicitly experimental per its own docs as of this build, but officially maintained by the Next.js team and actively developed; installed anyway per this ADR's own decision 5 reasoning. Re-check again at the next major Next.js upgrade.**
- ~~SEO-3's template placeholder syntax... deliberately not settled in this grilling session~~ — **resolved by this ADR's own addendum decision 8 before build: reuses `ADR-028` addendum decision 13's `{store_name}`/`{game_name}` convention exactly, implemented as `storefront/src/lib/seo.ts`'s `renderTemplate()`.**
- Decision 6's access model applies identically to `ADR-028`'s `reseller_branding` — if Phase 2's reseller self-service portal ever gets built, both tables need the same access-scoping treatment at the same time; don't solve it for one and forget the other. **Still open — unaffected by this build.**
- ~~Decision 3's `redirects` table needs a concrete execution mechanism chosen at build time...~~ **Resolved by addendum decision 9, built 2026-08-22 as `storefront/src/proxy.ts`** — not `middleware.ts`: this project's installed Next.js 16 has deprecated and renamed the file convention (confirmed via its own bundled docs, not assumed).

**Addendum, 2026-08-22 — the three deliberately-deferred items above resolved before build (quick follow-up round, same pattern as `ADR-025`'s own addendum), no scope changes to the 7 main decisions.**

8. **SEO-3's template placeholder syntax reuses `ADR-028` addendum decision 13's exact convention, not a new one invented for this ADR.** `{game_name}`/`{store_name}` tokens are substituted at storefront render time only (never at save time); any other brace sequence (a typo, an unrecognized token) is left verbatim, no error. One consistent templating rule across the whole app rather than two subtly different ones a future reader would have to keep straight.

9. **Redirects (decision 3) execute via Next.js's native `middleware.ts` — framework middleware, not a Vercel-specific product — checking each request's pathname against an in-memory cache of the `redirects` table, not a DB round-trip per request.** Chosen over a backend 404-fallback because this project's own deployment target (`ADR-020`) is a self-hosted droplet running `next start`, not Vercel's platform — `middleware.ts` runs identically there, it isn't an Edge-only or Vercel-only mechanism. The cache is populated from the storefront's own `getBranding()`-style backend fetch (`ADR-028` addendum precedent) and invalidated the same way `BrandingController::forgetCache()` already does on save — a `RedirectsController::forgetCache()` sibling, not a new invalidation pattern. A cache-miss (cold start, or the TTL just expired) costs one lookup; every other request in that window costs nothing beyond an in-memory array scan.

10. **UI placement: a new top-level admin nav item, "SEO"** (`/admin/seo`), not a fourth tab folded into `ADR-028`'s `/admin/settings`. Matches `prd.md`'s own §6.16/§6.17 split (SEO Management and Settings are two separate functional areas in the spec, not one) and keeps the Settings page from growing a fourth tab on top of its existing three plus the bulk-markup tool. Three sections on this one page: SEO Overview (decision 4's coverage checklist, read-only), Reseller SEO Settings (decision 2's `reseller_seo_settings` form — default meta/OG, template patterns, GA/FB/TikTok pixel IDs, custom scripts), Redirects (decision 3's table — add/edit/delete `from_path`/`to_path`/`status_code`). Per-game SEO (decision 1) stays exactly where decision 1 already put it — `EditGameModal` — this new page does not duplicate it.

**Consequence to track (addendum):** ~~`@next/third-parties`'s experimental status... still needs a fresh check at the actual build session~~ **done, see the main Consequence to track above.** ~~`RedirectsController::forgetCache()` (decision 9) needs the same discipline...~~ **Built as `SeoController::forgetCache()` (public controller, mirrors `BrandingController::forgetCache()` exactly), called from every admin write in `Admin\RedirectController`/`Admin\SeoScriptController`. The proxy's own in-memory cache (`src/proxy.ts`) is separately TTL-based (60s), not push-invalidated from the backend — a cold start or empty cache correctly falls through to "no redirect fires," not an error, confirmed by `NextResponse.next()` being the default path.**

**See ADR-042** for the SEO scope-widening decisions (originally this entry's Addendum 2 and Addendum 3, 2026-08-22) — moved out to their own entry since together they're an independent decision batch (structured data, scripts manager, crawler/robots management, sitemap, overview panels, per-game SEO UX, nav grouping), not a refinement of decisions 1-10 above.

**See ADR-043** for the `llms.txt` decision (originally this entry's Addendum 4, 2026-08-22) — moved out to its own entry since it's an independent decision batch, not a refinement of decisions 1-10 above.

## ADR-030: Digiflazz supplier integration — buyer-role adapter, prepaid games only (built 2026-08-25)

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-24 (grilled with the founder one decision at a time via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, before any code touched)

**Context:** The founder is negotiating with Digiflazz as a second supplier alongside Gamevion. Digiflazz is an H2H (head-to-head) aggregator; we connect as its **Buyer** through its REST API (`developer.digiflazz.com`, read live this session, not assumed — the full connection matrix for Jabber/API/FM/IRS/Otomax/etc. was reviewed, and only the API path applies to us). Scope was locked with the founder: **prepaid games only** (instant top-up), buyer role first. The **Seller** role (selling our own stock into Digiflazz's network — Digiflazz's buyers would order from us and we would expose an inbound endpoint plus a callback) was evaluated and deliberately rejected for now: we have no upstream inventory of our own to fulfill, we are ourselves a reseller, so the seller role has no business-model fit until we become a real distributor.

Digiflazz's relevant API surface (all JSON, all POST, responses wrapped in a `data` variable): `/v1/cek-saldo` (`cmd: deposit`), `/v1/price-list` (`cmd: prepaid`/`pasca`), `/v1/transaction` (topup). **The MD5 signature formula is per-endpoint, not one shared formula** — corrected during a founder-requested re-check of this ADR against the live docs, 2026-08-24: `cek-saldo` signs `md5(username + apiKey + "depo")`, `price-list` signs `md5(username + apiKey + "pricelist")`, and only `/v1/transaction` (topup, and its checkStatus re-submit) signs `md5(username + apiKey + ref_id)` — `ref_id` is our own unique reference there, which is a meaningful advantage over Gamevion (see ADR-032). Each adapter method must build its own literal signature string; assuming one formula across all three endpoints produces `rc: 41` (invalid signature) on `checkBalance()`/`listProducts()`. `price-list` is documented as **not real-time** (10-15 minutes stale) with an explicit recommendation to cache it in our own DB — exactly the existing `supplier_products` staging pattern. No player-validation endpoint exists (ADR-005's fallback applies to every game). Live test this session confirmed the first request returned `rc: 45 / "IP Anda tidak kami kenali"` — credentials and signature were accepted and the only blocker was the outbound-IP whitelist, which is precisely what the supplier wants to see to configure.

Key differences from Gamevion the adapter must absorb (ADR-006's own "never assume uniformity" principle): statuses are Indonesian (`Sukses`/`Pending`/`Gagal`) with `rc` codes; `createOrder` can return **Pending** (async — resolved later, see ADR-032); `checkStatus` is a re-submit of `/v1/transaction` with the same `ref_id` (an idempotent status query, **not** a new transaction — this closes the reference-number-lookup gap that makes ADR-026's `NeedsReview` unresolvable against Gamevion); IP whitelisting applies in both directions; game player-id input formats are **not documented** in the public API docs (must be verified live against the sandbox / with the supplier); two documented operational warnings — don't re-call the same transaction within 1 minute, and never re-submit a `ref_id` older than 90 days (it creates a NEW transaction) — are handled by ADR-032's guards.

**Decision:**

1. **New `DigiflazzAdapter` implementing `SupplierAdapter`** (buyer role, prepaid games only). Method mapping: `checkBalance()` → `/v1/cek-saldo`; `listProducts()` → `/v1/price-list` (`cmd: prepaid`); `createOrder()` → `/v1/transaction`; `checkStatus()` → `/v1/transaction` re-submitted with `ref_id` = `supplierRef`; `validatePlayer()` → `ValidationNotSupportedException` (ADR-005).
2. **The adapter stays protocol-faithful: `listProducts()` returns the full prepaid catalog.** The "games only" business filter lives in `ProductSyncService`, reading a game category/brand whitelist from `Supplier.api_config` — not in the adapter. Business policy (we only sell game top-up) is separated from supplier protocol.
3. **`testing: true` flag** driven by `services.digiflazz.testing` config, sent per-request only when true (mirrors Gamevion's `GAMEVION_SANDBOX` pattern).
4. **`max_price` deliberately not implemented now** — recorded as a deferred enhancement. `SupplierOrderRequest` carries no price information, so implementing it would require reshaping a stable seam for a feature whose margin risk is already guarded by price sync + ADR-025's floor/swing checks. Revisit only with a real need.
5. **`normalizeCustomerNo()` is config-driven** (`playerId` + optional `serverId`, configurable separator); the exact Digiflazz MLBB format is verified at `app:digiflazz-smoke-test` against the sandbox after the account is verified — the public docs do not document game player-id formats.
6. **Config + plumbing:** `config/services.php['digiflazz']` (env-based credentials, same pattern as Gamevion), optional `SUPPLIER_PROXY_URL` proxy for the outbound-IP whitelist (the pre-existing proxy seam), and the `CircuitBreakingSupplierAdapter` decorator wrapper (ADR-019) — the adapter itself is unchanged for circuit breaking.
7. **New `app:digiflazz-smoke-test`** (mirrors `GamevionSmokeTest`) and `tests/Feature/Services/Supplier/DigiflazzAdapterTest.php` (mirrors `GamevionAdapterTest`'s success/failure/status-mapping cases). Digiflazz's official prepaid test cases (`buyer_sku_code: xld10`) are the live-verification vehicle — **all four**, not three (corrected 2026-08-24 re-check): `087800001230`→Sukses, `087800001232`→Gagal, `087800001233`→Pending-then-callback-Sukses, `087800001234`→Pending-then-callback-Gagal. The fourth case is the one that actually exercises ADR-032's riskiest path (`Pending`→`Failed` via webhook, the exact double-compensation guard `VoucherController::storeFromOrder()`'s Failed-only gate protects) — omitting it from the smoke test/adapter test would leave that path never live-verified.
8. **The adapter normalizes raw statuses into `SupplierResponse`'s normalized outcome** (`delivered`/`pending`/`failure`) per ADR-032 — it never exposes `Sukses`/`Pending`/`Gagal` to business logic.

**Rationale:** Scope is prepaid games because that is the business (instant top-up); postpaid (PLN/PDAM/BPJS) and hotel APIs exist but are deliberately not implemented. Protocol-faithful adapter + policy-in-sync-layer keeps the adapter reusable across suppliers and the business filter changeable per supplier without touching protocol handling — the same ADAPT-1/3 reasoning that formalized `SupplierCatalogItem`. Deferring `max_price` avoids reshaping a stable seam for a safety net ADR-025 already provides. Everything Digiflazz-specific is absorbed inside the adapter or `api_config`, so no core service learns Digiflazz's name.

**Consequence to track:**
- This ADR records design intent only — update `docs/prd.md` §14/§15 once this ships (same convention as ADR-025/026).
- Digiflazz prices are **IDR** — see ADR-033 for conversion.
- The Pending state + webhook/poll finalization are **ADR-032**'s work, not this ADR's.
- Outbound IP (or the proxy's IP) must be whitelisted at Digiflazz; and Digiflazz's `52.74.250.133` must be whitelisted on our side before webhooks can be accepted (ADR-032).
- The 90-day re-submit rule is enforced in ADR-032's reconcile guards, not here.

## ADR-031: Multi-supplier routing — `SupplierAdapterFactory` + one-Package-one-supplier (built 2026-08-25)

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-24 (grilled with the founder one decision at a time via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, before any code touched)

**Context:** `AppServiceProvider` currently binds a single global `SupplierAdapter` to Gamevion — its own comment calls this *"a deliberate placeholder, not the final shape"* (`AppServiceProvider.php:27-31`). The data model is already multi-supplier-ready: `Package` carries `supplier_id` + `supplier_package_ref`, `Order` carries `supplier_id` + `supplier_product_ref`, and `CheckoutService` already stores both at checkout. What does not exist is **resolution** — `OrderFulfillmentService::fulfill()` calls `$this->supplier->createOrder(...)` against the one global adapter without ever reading `$order->supplier_id`, so a Digiflazz-backed package would today still be submitted to Gamevion. ADR-030 (second supplier) makes this gap real.

**Decision:**

1. **New `SupplierAdapterFactory`** that resolves an adapter implementation by supplier slug/id through container bindings (`supplier-adapter.<slug>`), mirroring the proven `PaymentGatewayFactory` precedent on the payment side. Throws `UnsupportedSupplierException` for unregistered slugs. The single global `SupplierAdapter` binding is removed; `PaymentGateway::class` keeps its own default-binding asymmetry only because webhook URLs are inherently gateway-specific (unchanged).
2. **One Package = one supplier.** Equivalent denominations across suppliers are separate `Package` rows (see ADR-034 for storefront dedup). **No auto-failover for MVP** — deliberately; an order's supplier is fixed at package-curation time, never decided at delivery.
3. **`OrderFulfillmentService::fulfill()` and `OrderResendService` resolve the adapter by `$order->supplier_id`**, not a globally injected adapter. The `e2e` environment's `FakeSupplierAdapter` binding (ADR-023 decision #6) stays exactly as it is.
4. **Sync commands loop over suppliers:** `app:sync-supplier-products` and `SyncSupplierPricesJob` iterate active `Supplier` rows, resolving each via the factory (the existing hardcoded `firstOrCreate(['slug' => 'gamevion'])` stopgap becomes a loop). `ProductSyncService`/`PackagePriceSyncService` already take a `Supplier` and operate per-supplier via `supplier_id` — unchanged.
5. **Invariant: no supplier name appears in core services** (fulfillment, order-status, sync, pricing, checkout, reconcile). Only adapters, per-supplier webhook controllers, config/services, and tests are supplier-named. Supplier quirks live in adapters and `Supplier.api_config`.

**Rationale:** This mirrors the payment side's already-proven factory pattern rather than inventing a new one. One-Package-one-supplier is the cheapest correct routing model — the schema already supports it, it keeps fulfillment deterministic, and it avoids the money-critical complexity of failover. A future supplier C costs exactly: one adapter + one config block + one factory binding + one thin webhook controller — zero changes to the state machine, fulfillment, sync, or pricing. The invariant (decision 5) is what makes that true; without it, "add a supplier" degrades into "fork the services."

**Consequence to track:**
- **Verify (don't change) the latent Gap-X behavior** during reconcile generalization: `ReconcilePendingDeliveriesCommand::retryStuckProcessing()` re-dispatches `FulfillOrderJob` for `Processing`+null-`supplier_ref` orders, but `FulfillOrderJob` catches `InvalidOrderTransitionException` (`FulfillOrderJob.php:67`) and `startDelivery()` rejects `Processing` — so that re-dispatch may be a no-op. It may also be unreachable in practice because `fulfill()` runs inside a single transaction (a hard crash rolls back to `NotStarted`). Verify with the existing tests; do not alter behavior in this ADR.
- Circuit-breaker names must become per-supplier (currently hardcoded `'gamevion'` in `AppServiceProvider`).

---

## ADR-032: Async supplier delivery — `DeliveryStatus::Pending` + normalized `SupplierResponse` outcome + webhook & poll finalization (built 2026-08-25)

**Status:** Accepted (design) — 2026-08-24 (grilled with the founder one decision at a time via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling`, before any code touched)

**Context:** Digiflazz `createOrder` can return `status: "Pending"` (`rc: 03`) — the transaction is accepted but not yet delivered, resolving later via webhook/callback. Our delivery state machine (`DeliveryStatus`: `NotStarted`/`Processing`/`Delivered`/`Failed`/`NeedsReview`) has **no way to hold an order in "supplier accepted, awaiting async completion"**. `Processing` is transient — set and resolved inside `fulfill()`'s same transaction, never a persistent waiting state. Gamevion resolves synchronously (createOrder success → `Delivered`); its "processing" is a raw API value never persisted as a `DeliveryStatus`.

Mapping Pending→`Delivered` would lie to the customer. Mapping Pending→`Failed` risks **double compensation**: `VoucherController::storeFromOrder()` issues store-credit on `Failed`-only (the ADR-026 decision 4c precedent), so a top-up that later completes would give the customer both the credit *and* a refund voucher. `SupplierResponse` (`SupplierResponse.php`) currently distinguishes only `success`/`failure` — there is no "accepted but pending" outcome, so routing by supplier name would violate ADAPT-1/3. The founder chose **both** webhook (primary) and poll (backup).

**Decision:**

1. **New `DeliveryStatus::Pending`** — "supplier accepted, awaiting final outcome". `Processing` stays the transient in-flight state (Gamevion's sync path unchanged). New transitions: `Processing→Pending`, `Pending→Delivered`, `Pending→Failed`.
2. **`SupplierResponse` gains a normalized outcome** — additive, backward-compatible: `success()` (delivered now), new `pending()` (accepted, async), `failure()`. Each adapter maps its raw statuses (Gamevion always `success`; Digiflazz `Sukses`→`success`, `Pending`→`pending`, `Gagal`→`failure`). `fulfill()` branches on the normalized outcome, **never on supplier identity**. This is the single additive interface change the whole Digiflazz plan needs.
3. **`OrderFulfillmentService::finalizePendingDelivery(order, outcome)`** — the one money path out of `Pending`: `lockForUpdate()` + transition guard + `creditProfit()` + voucher `commit()` (mirrors `markDeliveredManually`). Idempotent (a second call observes `Delivered` and is rejected) and covered by a real concurrency test (duplicate webhook delivery).
4. **Webhook (primary):** a thin `DigiflazzWebhookController` — verifies `X-Hub-Signature` (`sha1=HMAC(body, secret)`, secret from config), handles `X-Digiflazz-Event` `create`/`update` (ignores the hotel-only `resend`), maps the payload's `ref_id` (= our `reference_number`) to the order, and calls the shared `finalizePendingDelivery`. Digiflazz IP `52.74.250.133` is whitelisted on our side. Webhook controllers stay per-supplier (URL + signature verification differ per supplier) but all converge on the same finalize.
5. **Poll (backup):** `ReconcilePendingDeliveriesCommand` gains a generic branch — stale `Pending` orders (per-supplier `pending_stale_minutes`, default ~10) dispatch a new `CheckSupplierDeliveryJob`, which resolves the adapter by `order.supplier_id`, calls `checkStatus`, and routes the normalized outcome through the same finalize. Never calls a supplier synchronously from a scheduled command (ADR-014). Still-`Pending` stays for the next run.
6. **Operational guards are config, not hardcoded branches** (`Supplier.api_config`): `status_check_min_interval` (Digiflazz warns against re-calling the same transaction within 1 minute — reconcile cadence respects it) and `max_reconcile_age_days` (never re-submit a `ref_id` older than 90 days — Digiflazz creates a NEW transaction — such orders are auto-flagged for manual review instead).
7. **Deliberately not opened:** voucher issuance from `Pending` stays `Failed`-only (ADR-026 decision 4c) — the double-compensation guard is preserved.

**Rationale:** A typed `Pending` state plus a normalized outcome on `SupplierResponse` keeps the state machine honest and supplier-agnostic — a future async supplier (webhook-only, poll-only, or both) needs exactly this and nothing else, and no core service ever learns a supplier's name. Webhook-primary + poll-backup covers missed webhooks without any single delivery mechanism being load-bearing. Config-driven guards keep supplier operational constraints (1-minute, 90-day) out of generic code. The single `finalizePendingDelivery` money path guarantees credit and voucher-commit happen exactly once regardless of which mechanism resolves the order.

**Consequence to track:**
- Audit every `match`/`switch` over `DeliveryStatus` — `OrderController`'s status filters, `OrderStatusService`'s transition guards, and the frontend display mapping — for the new `Pending` case (the same checklist ADR-026 recorded for `NeedsReview`; TypeScript exhaustiveness needs the same check).
- Storefront Track Order renders `Processing` and `Pending` with the **same customer-friendly copy** ("topup sedang diproses" — they mean the same thing to a customer); the admin panel shows raw states.
- New concurrency test for `finalizePendingDelivery` under duplicate webhook delivery (real-MySQL suite, per `backend/CLAUDE.md` convention).
- `checkStatus` semantics now genuinely differ per supplier (Gamevion: their invoice number; Digiflazz: our `ref_id`) — the `SupplierAdapter` interface already accommodates this, but the reconcile command must resolve the adapter per order rather than assume one shape.
