## ADR-041: Checkout-level idempotency key — client-generated key, unique DB constraint, replay/resume branching (built 2026-07-29)

**Status:** Accepted, built — 2026-07-29 (grilled via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling` before implementation). Split out from ADR-019's addenda chain (2026-08-27 docs refactor) for readability — see ADR-019's cross-reference.

**Context:** ADR-019's fix-now list closed most resilience gaps but explicitly left one open: a retried `POST /api/checkout` (customer double-click, client-side timeout retry) mints a brand-new `order_number` each time, which Xendit's own `reference_id` dedupe can't catch. This became a pre-requisite, not a deferred item, once the founder planned the platform's first deliberate real end-to-end purchase-workflow proof (Xendit test-mode + Gamevion production) — a network hiccup during that test is exactly when a double-order is most likely, so the known gap had to close before the test, not after.

**Decision (verbatim from ADR-019's original addendum):**

**Addendum — checkout-level idempotency key shipped, 2026-07-29 (later same session, new day's work — surfaced as a pre-requisite, not deferred further, while planning the platform's first deliberate real end-to-end purchase-workflow proof: Xendit test-mode + Gamevion production, grilled via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling` before implementation, same discipline as every other ADR-014-through-019 decision):** closes the one item this ADR's fix-now list explicitly left open above — a retried `POST /api/checkout` (customer double-click, client-side timeout retry) minting a brand-new `order_number` each time, which Xendit's own `reference_id` dedupe can't catch. Founder's own framing for why now, not later: about to run a real production-money test (Gamevion in production mode) for the first time — a network hiccup during *that* session is exactly when a double-order is most likely, so the known gap had to close before the test, not after.

Design (grilled decision, not assumed): a client-generated `idempotency_key` (storefront: `crypto.randomUUID()`, generated once when the Review Modal opens, unchanged across a resubmit of that same attempt — see `OrderForm.tsx`'s `idempotencyKeyRef`), stamped onto the Order **at creation** (not after payment succeeds) under a new `orders.checkout_idempotency_key` (nullable, **unique**) column — reserved this early specifically so a genuine race between two near-simultaneous requests carrying the same key fails one of them at the DB layer (`23000` unique-violation, caught as `DuplicateCheckoutAttemptException`), not just at an app-level `SELECT` that both requests could pass before either commits.

`CheckoutController::store()` now looks up `Order::where('checkout_idempotency_key', ...)` **before** re-running player-validation/blacklist/velocity checks (an Order tagged with the key already passed those in the request that created it — re-running would be redundant at best, double-count a velocity hit at worst) and branches three ways:
1. **Key not found** → normal `CheckoutService::initiate()` flow, now stamping the key at creation.
2. **Found, `payment_ref` already set** → pure idempotent replay (`200`, not `201`) — the same order/payment_actions a fresh checkout would have returned, no new Order, no second gateway call.
3. **Found, `payment_ref` still null** → the earlier attempt's Order was created but its payment call failed (gateway rejection, or the process died in between). New `CheckoutService::resume(Order, PaymentGateway, channelCode, channelProperties)` retries **only** the payment leg against that same Order, reusing its own already-snapshotted `final_amount`/customer fields (ORD-9 — never recomputed) — Xendit's own `reference_id` dedupe (`order_number`, unchanged) still applies as a second layer if that earlier attempt secretly reached Xendit despite failing to persist locally.

Deliberately **not** solved, recorded as an accepted residual rather than silently dropped: a race narrower than the unique-constraint window above — two requests that both pass the initial lookup in the same few milliseconds, before either's `INSERT` commits — resolves correctly (loser gets `DuplicateCheckoutAttemptException`, refetches the winner) but the winner's response may still show a null `payment_ref` if returned mid-flight. Judged not worth a retry-loop/polling mechanism for a window this narrow.

Shipped and verified: migration + `Order::$fillable`, `CreateCheckoutRequest` (`idempotency_key` required), `CheckoutRequest` DTO, `CheckoutService::initiate()`/`resume()`/`DuplicateCheckoutAttemptException`, `CheckoutController`'s lookup/replay/resume branches, `storefront/`'s `checkout.ts`/`OrderForm.tsx`. 6 new `CheckoutControllerTest` cases + 3 new `CheckoutServiceTest` cases (replay, resume-after-failure, duplicate-key-throws, distinct-keys-stay-distinct, missing-key-rejected) — full backend suite **447/447 passing** (up from 396). `npx tsc --noEmit`/`next build`/`eslint` all clean on `storefront/`. Migration run against the real local dev DB (sqlite — confirmed via `PRAGMA index_list`, not assumed), closing the gotcha `AGENTS.md` itself warns about (a new migration only auto-runs against test DBs by default).

## ADR-042: SEO module scope widened — structured data, scripts manager, crawler/robots management, sitemap & overview panels, per-game SEO UX (built 2026-08-22)

**Status:** Accepted, built — 2026-08-22 (grilled decision-by-decision against a competitor-product reference, none blindly copied). Split out from ADR-029's Addendum 2 and Addendum 3 (2026-08-27 docs refactor) for readability — see ADR-029's cross-reference. Addendum 3 (decision 21) is folded into this entry rather than given its own, since it's a direct follow-up refinement to decision 14 below, not an independent decision batch.

**Context:** The founder asked for a critique, not a copy, after reviewing a competing product's SEO module (screenshots supplied by the founder, "KeroxShop" — a separate, unrelated admin panel, not this project's own data) — which of the reference's ideas are real upgrades versus scope creep or a design mistake ADR-029 already deliberately avoided. Each item below was judged on its own merits against this codebase's existing conventions, not adopted because the reference had it.

**Decision (verbatim from ADR-029's original Addendum 2 and Addendum 3):**

**Addendum 2, 2026-08-22 (same day, later) — scope widened after reviewing a competing product's SEO module (screenshots supplied by the founder, "KeroxShop" — a separate, unrelated admin panel, not this project's own data) for genuinely adoptable ideas, grilled decision by decision, none blindly copied.**

**Context:** The founder asked for a critique, not a copy — which of the reference's ideas are real upgrades versus scope creep or a design mistake this ADR already deliberately avoided. Each item below was judged on its own merits against this codebase's existing conventions, not adopted because the reference had it.

11. **Per-game SEO's *UI* moves out of `EditGameModal` into its own list+edit screen on the new SEO page — decision 1's data placement (`Game.seo_*` columns) is unchanged, only where it's edited.** A dedicated `Game SEO` list (search, complete/incomplete/missing filter, per-row completeness) with its own edit view mirrors this codebase's own established list-page-plus-edit pattern (`/admin/vouchers`, `/admin/withdrawals`) better than bolting SEO fields onto an unrelated catalog-editing modal — the same reasoning that already justified splitting `reseller_footer_settings` out of `reseller_branding` (`ADR-028` addendum decision 10) applies again here: a distinct editing concern gets its own surface.

12. **Structured data (JSON-LD) added — `Product`/`Organization`/`Breadcrumb` schema toggles on `reseller_seo_settings`, plus `schema_brand`/`schema_category` columns on `Game`.** Real rich-snippet value or search-result quality, not a vanity add. No new dependency — JSON-LD is a `<script type="application/ld+json">` tag with a computed object, natively supported by `generateMetadata()`'s existing approach (decision 5). `schema-dts` (types only, zero runtime cost) is worth adding for authoring safety, not required.

13. **Scripts manager replaces decision 2's flat `custom_head_script`/`custom_body_end_script` column pair with a new `seo_scripts` table** (`name`, `location` enum `head`/`body_end`, `code`, `priority` int, `reseller_id` nullable — null means global, `is_active`). A real upgrade over two flat fields: ordered, multiple scripts, reseller-scoped even with only one reseller today — the identical "build the real shape ahead of a stated future direction" reasoning `ADR-028`'s `reseller_branding` already used. Basic pre-save validation (well-formed `<script>`/tag balance, not a full HTML parser) mirrors the reference's own "Validate Script" affordance.

14. **Crawler / `robots.txt` management added** — a new `crawler_rules`-shaped config (per-bot allow/block covering search engines, social-preview bots, and AI-training bots, plus crawl-delay and disallow-path lists), rendered through Next.js's **native** `app/robots.ts` (`MetadataRoute.Robots`) — no library, the framework already generates `robots.txt` from a typed config object. Genuinely timely (AI-scraper blocking is a real, current concern), not scope creep for its own sake. A curated default bot list plus an "Add Custom Rule" escape hatch, matching the reference's own pattern, rather than trying to enumerate every bot that will ever exist.

15. **Redirects gain a `hit_count` column, incremented every time the `middleware.ts` lookup (decision 9) actually fires one.** Cheap, real operational value — shows which old URLs are still being followed versus safe to prune. Regex matching and CSV bulk-import (also in the reference) are explicitly **not** adopted — exact-path matching (decision 3, unchanged) already covers the realistic slug-rename case, and neither earns its complexity for a single-reseller MVP with a handful of redirects; revisit only if a real need surfaces, not preemptively.

16. **Sitemap generation is fully automatic via Next.js's native `app/sitemap.ts`, with no admin-configurable priority/changefreq controls — explicitly rejecting that part of the reference.** Google has long since stopped meaningfully using `<priority>`/`<changefreq>` — exposing them as admin knobs would be config with no real SEO effect, the same "don't invent a metric without real basis" reasoning this ADR's own decision 4 already applied to the vanity score below. "No admin controls" doesn't mean "invisible" — the SEO Overview page (decision 17) gets one read-only status line (URL count) plus a direct link to `/sitemap.xml`, so the admin can actually see what's in it without needing a shell/curl. A status line, not a setting — nothing on it is editable.

17. **The reference's single weighted "Overall Score % + letter grade" is explicitly rejected, not adopted — it's exactly the vanity metric this ADR's own decision 4 already ruled out.** Its **Recommendations** (actionable, severity-tagged suggestions with a "Fix Now" jump-link) and **Recent Issues** (a scannable, per-row-actionable table) panels *are* adopted for the Overview page — a real improvement over a static checklist alone, and consistent with this codebase's existing severity-pill dashboard convention (`/admin/blacklist`'s blocked-attempt history). Both are computed views over existing data (`Game.seo_*` completeness, redirect/script counts) — no new storage.

18. **Per-game SEO edit view gains: character counters (70/160, matching Google's real truncation points), a "Use Game Image" button that copies the game's existing catalog image into `seo_og_image` instead of requiring a re-paste, and a `no_index` boolean column on `Game`** (renders a per-game `noindex` meta directive). All cheap, all real value, all still inside decision 1's existing `Game.seo_*` scope — `no_index` is the only new column among the three.

19. **The reference's "Analytics Permissions" (a platform-level allow/disallow gate before a reseller may configure their own GA/FB/TikTok pixel) is explicitly rejected.** Decision 6 already established there is no reseller self-service portal — a permission gate for a reseller managing their own tracking solves a problem that doesn't exist yet in this codebase's single-reseller reality; revisit only alongside Phase 2's actual self-service portal, per decision 6's own already-recorded reasoning.

20. **Admin nav placement: "SEO" becomes a collapsible nav *group*, not a single link** — sub-items Overview / Global Settings / Meta Templates / Game SEO / Redirects / Scripts / Crawler. `AppSidebar.tsx` has no existing collapsible-group pattern (every current item is a flat single link) — this is new sidebar UI work the build session needs to add, not a reuse of an existing mechanism.

**Addendum 3, 2026-08-22 (same day, immediately after build+browser-verification) — one refinement, founder-requested during the verification walkthrough.**

21. **`crawler_rules.disallow_paths` (per-row) is joined by a new shared `reseller_seo_settings.crawler_default_disallow_paths` — a single list merged into every `is_allowed` bot's own disallow set at render time (`SeoController::robots()`), covering bots added to `crawler_rules` later too, with zero per-row re-entry.** Surfaced live: the founder asked "so kalau nak block satu route untuk semua bot, kena update satu-satu ke?" while walking through the Crawler page — the honest answer given the ADR's own design (per-row `disallow_paths`) was yes, because a robots.txt `User-agent` block never inherits from `*`; a named bot with its own block ignores whatever `*` disallows entirely. Rather than accept that duplication, added one shared field instead. Seeded with `['/order/status', '/api']` (`CrawlerRuleSeeder`) — a specific customer's order-tracking page (no SEO value, a real privacy concern if indexed) and this app's own Next.js route handlers (not content). `Admin\SeoController::updateSettings()` now calls `PublicSeoController::forgetRobotsCache()` in addition to its own `forgetCache()`, since this field lives on `reseller_seo_settings` but is consumed by the `robots()` endpoint's own separately-cached response.

**Consequence to track (addendum 2):**
- `seo_scripts`' validation (decision 13) is deliberately basic (tag-balance, not a full parser) — don't over-build a real HTML/JS validator for what is, ultimately, a trusted-admin-only text field. **Built exactly this way, 2026-08-22 (`SaveSeoScriptRequest::withValidator()`).**
- ~~`app/robots.ts`'s typed config shape (decision 14) needs to be checked against this project's actual installed Next.js version's docs before building...~~ **Checked before writing it, 2026-08-22 — confirmed against `storefront/node_modules/next/dist/docs`, matches the ADR's assumed shape exactly.**
- ~~Decision 11 changes *where* per-game SEO is edited but not its data shape — if `EditGameModal` already gained any SEO-adjacent UI before this is built, reconcile then...~~ **Checked before build — `EditGameModal.tsx` still had zero SEO fields, no reconciliation needed.**
- ~~This addendum, like the ADR it amends, is design-only — nothing built yet.~~ **Built 2026-08-22 — see `docs/prd.md` §14.**

**Consequence to track (addendum 3):** `crawler_default_disallow_paths` lives on the reseller-scoped `reseller_seo_settings` table, but `crawler_rules` itself is deliberately global (decision 14's own migration doc comment — one robots.txt per domain). Today, with exactly one reseller/domain, merging the one settings row's defaults into the one global rule set is correct by construction. If Phase 2 ever onboards a second reseller with its own domain, this merge needs a real decision — which reseller's defaults apply to a global rule set that doesn't itself know which domain served the request — not an extension of today's single-tenant shortcut. Flag alongside decision 6's already-recorded Phase-2 access-model gap, not a new category of unresolved question.

## ADR-043: `llms.txt` — auto-generated AI/LLM-context route (built 2026-08-22)

**Status:** Accepted, built — 2026-08-22. Split out from ADR-029's Addendum 4 (2026-08-27 docs refactor) for readability — see ADR-029's cross-reference.

**Context:** Founder asked directly, in chat, whether llms.txt (llmstxt.org's proposed AI/LLM-context convention) belongs alongside robots.txt/sitemap.ts, since it's another crawler-facing file. Scoped down to two quick decisions rather than a full grilling pass — genuinely small surface, not a multi-table feature.

**Decision (verbatim from ADR-029's original Addendum 4):**

**Addendum 4, 2026-08-22 (same day, later) — founder asked directly, in chat, whether llms.txt (llmstxt.org's proposed AI/LLM-context convention) belongs here too, since it's another crawler-facing file like robots.txt/sitemap.ts. Scoped down to two quick decisions rather than a full grilling pass — genuinely small surface, not a multi-table feature.**

22. **`storefront/src/app/llms.txt/route.ts` — fully auto-generated from existing catalog/branding data, no new admin-authored field or table.** Same choice `app/sitemap.ts` already made for the same reason: nothing to drift out of sync with the real catalog, no second place for the founder to remember to update. Summary line falls back `reseller_seo_settings.default_meta_description` → `reseller_branding.description` → a generic hardcoded sentence; game list and static-page links pulled from the same `listGames()`/`SITE_URL` this app's `sitemap.ts` already uses.
23. **Only `/llms.txt` (the concise root convention) — `/llms-full.txt` deliberately not built.** llms.txt itself is a young, not-yet-officially-adopted proposal (unlike robots.txt, which every real crawler already respects); building a second, less-established variant on top of an already-unproven one isn't justified yet. Revisit only if real adoption signal shows up.

## ADR-044: Zod runtime schema validation at the admin/storefront API boundary (built 2026-08-27)

**Status:** Accepted, built — 2026-08-27 (grilled via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling` before implementation, three rounds).

**Context:** Neither `admin/` nor `storefront/` has ever had a runtime schema-validation layer at the API boundary, despite `AGENTS.md`'s own standing rule ("Zod/equivalent at the frontend's API boundary") — `grep` for `zod`/`yup`/`joi` across both apps' `package.json` returned nothing, and neither app has a single email/phone regex or form-schema check anywhere. Every request payload (`CheckoutPayload`, etc.) is a compile-time-only TypeScript `interface`; every response is blind-cast (`payload as T` in `apiFetch<T>()`) with zero runtime check that the backend actually returned that shape. This is **not** a security gap — every mutating backend route already has full `FormRequest` coverage (44/44) and money is never trusted from the client regardless (ORD-9) — it's a client-side UX and contract-drift-detection gap: a typo currently round-trips to the backend and back before the customer sees an error, and a backend response-shape change would fail silently (wrong/undefined field read) rather than surface anywhere.

Fact-finding before the decision: `storefront/src/lib/api-client.ts` has 2 commits, both from initial scaffold (2026-07-23/26) — essentially frozen since. `OrderForm.tsx`/`checkout.ts` (the checkout-critical files) are touched roughly every 1-2 weeks (7 and 5 commits respectively, last 2026-08-14) — an "opportunistic, only when the file is already being touched" rollout would reach them fine on its own. Neither app has a toast library or any error-monitoring SaaS (Sentry etc.) — the established error-UX pattern is a local `useState<string|null>` populated in a `catch` block, rendered as an inline `<p>` banner (`storefront`'s `Step1AccountInfo.tsx`/`ReviewModal.tsx`, `admin`'s `vouchers/page.tsx`/`withdrawals/page.tsx` — identical shape both apps). Scope-sizing: storefront has 8 files / ~16 functions consuming `apiFetch`/`apiUpload`; admin has 17 files / ~120 functions — a ~7-8x larger surface, making a single big-bang rollout across both apps in one PR an unreasonable lift for admin specifically.

**Decision:**

1. **Add `zod` (latest stable) as a dependency to both `admin/` and `storefront/`.** No shared package/workspace between the two apps (deliberate divergence already established by `api-client.ts` itself, per ADR-011's guest-checkout-vs-Bearer-auth split) — schema duplication across the two apps for overlapping shapes is accepted, not solved with new shared-package infra, matching the existing precedent rather than opening an unrelated monorepo decision inside this ADR.
2. **Storefront: full rollout now, all ~16 `apiFetch`/`apiUpload` consumer functions** (`checkout.ts`, `catalog.ts`, `vouchers.ts`, and the rest of `storefront/src/lib`) — small enough surface to do in one pass, and includes the highest-value target (checkout) immediately rather than waiting for it to be "opportunistically" touched.
3. **Admin: convention-only this ADR, no mass migration.** Same opportunistic trigger `ADR-038` already established for the PrimeReact migration — a file already being touched for an unrelated reason gets zod added to its API calls as part of that same change; a live, tested screen is never migrated solely to add validation. No new lint/CI enforcement — pure discipline, matching this repo's existing solo-founder governance model.
4. **Both request-side and response-side validation, in scope together** — a request schema validates form payload before `apiFetch` is called (client-side UX only, never a security boundary — the backend `FormRequest` remains sole authority); a response schema replaces the current `payload as T` blind cast with `schema.parse()`.
5. **Response schemas run in non-strict (passthrough/strip-unknown) mode and fail soft.** An unrecognized-but-harmless extra field the backend adds later must never crash checkout; a genuine mismatch (missing/wrong-typed field) logs and falls back to using the raw payload as-is rather than throwing — response validation's job here is contract-drift *detection*, not a new production failure mode on the money path.
6. **`z.infer<typeof Schema>` becomes the source of truth for request/response types**, replacing hand-written `interface`s (`CheckoutPayload`, `CheckoutResult`, `ValidatePlayerResult`, etc.) in the files it touches — a schema and a separately-maintained interface would just be two copies of the same fact able to drift from each other, which is the exact problem this ADR exists to close.
7. **Schemas are colocated in the same file as the function that uses them** (e.g. `CheckoutPayloadSchema` inside `checkout.ts`, next to `submitCheckout()`) — no new `lib/schemas/` directory. Matches this codebase's existing pattern (the interfaces they replace already lived inline).
8. **New backend endpoint, `POST /api/client-errors`** — public (no auth; storefront is guest-checkout with no auth concept, and reusing this same endpoint from admin rather than building a second authenticated one keeps this small), throttled (reusing `ADR-014`'s `throttle:` pattern), with its own `FormRequest` per `AGENTS.md`'s "every mutating route gets a FormRequest" rule, accepting `{schema, path, error}` and writing it via `Log::warning` — mirrors `CheckoutController`'s existing structured-logging shape. Purpose is narrow: give the founder backend-log visibility into response-schema drift reports (item 5) that would otherwise only ever appear in a customer's own browser console, invisible to anyone. This is a small bespoke log sink for one specific event type, **not** a general error-monitoring/observability platform (no Sentry-equivalent scope) — it does not catch arbitrary JS exceptions, has no dashboard, and isn't intended to.

**Rationale:** Every piece of this decision traces back to something already established in this codebase rather than inventing new conventions — the opportunistic-rollout trigger (item 3) mirrors `ADR-038`, the FormRequest-per-mutating-route rule (item 8) mirrors `AGENTS.md`'s own standing rule, the inline-banner error surface (item 4/5's UX) reuses the pattern already live in both apps, and the schema-duplication-across-apps trade (item 1) matches `api-client.ts`'s own precedent. The one genuinely new piece of infra is the `/api/client-errors` endpoint (item 8), deliberately scoped as narrowly as possible — a single throttled log sink, not a monitoring platform — specifically to avoid solving a much bigger problem (general frontend observability) inside an ADR whose actual purpose is boundary validation.

**Consequence to track:** Admin's ~120-function surface remains fully unvalidated until individual files are opportunistically touched — unlike storefront (item 2, done in full now), there is no guarantee admin's higher-risk mutating screens (Withdrawals, Vouchers, Price Sync) get zod coverage on any particular timeline. If a real incident traces back to an unvalidated admin form, that's the signal to revisit item 3 rather than continuing to wait opportunistically. Also track: `/api/client-errors` (item 8) is new unauthenticated public surface — its throttle configuration needs the same periodic sanity-check this codebase already gives its other public-throttled routes, so it can't become a spam/log-flood vector.

**Consequence to track (addendum 4):** llms.txt has no confirmed, universal consumer today the way robots.txt does — Google/Bing/social-preview bots are proven; which AI systems, if any, actually fetch and use `/llms.txt` is still an open question industry-wide. Built because it's cheap and harmless (a markdown GET route, `force-dynamic`, no new storage), not because adoption is proven. If the convention is abandoned by the community, this route costs nothing to leave in place or remove later — no data model depends on it.

## ADR-045: Admin Dashboard — DASH-1..6, `orders.delivered_at`, and a per-metric self-documenting `definition` convention

**Status:** Accepted, built — 2026-08-27 (grilled via `/mattpocock-skills:grilling` before implementation, four rounds, 27 pinned decisions).

**Context:** `docs/prd.md` §6.2 (DASH-1..6) has sat unbuilt since the project's foundation — `admin/src/app/admin/page.tsx` (the route every login lands on, per `AppSidebar.tsx`'s existing "Dashboard" nav entry) is still literally the placeholder scaffold from day one, its own doc comment reading "DASH-1..DASH-6 ... come later — this is deliberately just 'who am I'". `foundation-security.md` §6 and `prd.md` §9 both name the per-supplier circuit-breaker display as an explicit MVP requirement, and `App\Services\CircuitBreaker\CircuitBreaker::state()` (ADR-019) was built specifically anticipating this screen but has never been wired to anything.

This ADR exists because Dashboard's obvious-looking requirements hide the same category of landmine Reports (RPT-1..3, no ADR of its own — see that build-log entry) found before it: metrics that look like a one-line COUNT/SUM actually need a real pinned definition (which timestamp, which table, cohort vs. snapshot) or they'll quietly compute something the founder didn't ask for. Unlike Reports, this ADR **is** numbered — Reports' decisions were entirely self-contained to `ReportService`/`ReportController`, consumed nowhere else; Dashboard's decisions cross-reference and reuse several existing seams (`ReportService`, `CircuitBreaker`, the `delivery_reconciliation` config, `OrderStatusService`) and add a new one (`orders.delivered_at`) that future sessions may build on, so a stable numbered reference point earns its keep here in a way it didn't for Reports.

Scope: **all six** DASH-1..6 requirements, built in one pass — founder's explicit call after weighing the alternative (DASH-1/2 only now, DASH-3..6 in a later grilled session) against building the dashboard route once instead of revisiting the same file twice.

**Decision:**

### DASH-1 — KPI cards (Sales / Orders / Profit / Vouchers Today, vs. yesterday)

1. **"Refunds Today" is renamed "Vouchers Issued Today."** The literal PRD wording directly conflicts with ADR-004 (no cash refunds, ever — the only two resolutions for a failed order are retry-delivery or Voucher issuance). Same category of fix Reports already made (dropping a reference design's non-applicable "Refund Rate"/"Chargeback Rate" tiles) — rename to the concept that actually exists here instead of faking the literal wording.
2. **"Vouchers Issued Today" counts Path B (order-triggered) vouchers only, not Path A (admin standalone).** Path B is the real compensation-for-a-failed-order signal this tile exists to show; Path A vouchers (promo/goodwill) are a different business event that would muddy it.
3. **Sales/Orders/Profit Today reuse `ReportService`'s existing pinned definitions verbatim** — ledger-sourced profit (never `Order.platform_profit`/`reseller_profit` directly), `payment_status=Paid` scoped by `paid_at` (never `created_at`), `is_test` excluded, Asia/Kuala_Lumpur day boundary. No new definition invented; `DashboardService` calls into `ReportService` for this leg rather than duplicating its logic.
4. **"vs. yesterday" renders as a percentage with an up/down arrow, colored green/red** (consistent with the `dataviz`-skill palette convention already used on `/admin/reports`'s trend charts). When yesterday's value for that metric is `0`, render **"New"** instead of computing a percentage (avoids an infinite/`NaN` result).

### DASH-2 — System Health

5. **Supplier API status is derived, never live-pinged.** Reads `CircuitBreaker::state()` (Closed/Open) per real `SupplierAdapter` implementation — no on-demand network call to the supplier on dashboard load, both because that would blow the §9 NFR's 2-second budget and because pinging a struggling supplier on every admin page load is exactly the retry-storm behavior the circuit breaker exists to prevent.
6. **No new "last checked" timestamp is added.** `CircuitBreaker` only stores `openedAt` (when it tripped), nothing for the closed-state "last successful call" case. Display state only (plus remaining cooldown seconds when Open) — adding new tracking for a "last checked: Xm ago" label is scope creep for a first cut, not required by DASH-2's own wording.
7. **"Stuck orders" reuses the existing `delivery_reconciliation` config (`DELIVERY_RECONCILIATION_STALE_AFTER_MINUTES`, default 15; `PENDING_STALE_MINUTES`, default 10), not a new dashboard-specific threshold.** These are the exact same numbers `ReconcilePendingDeliveriesCommand::retryStuckProcessing()` already uses to decide "stale enough to act on" — reusing them means Dashboard's "stuck" and the reconciliation job's "stale" can never silently drift apart into two different definitions of the same word. Rendered as **one combined count**: `DeliveryStatus::NeedsReview` (confirmed-ambiguous) + `Processing` orders older than the stale-after threshold + `Pending` orders older than the pending-stale threshold. Click-through target is `/admin/orders`'s existing `needs_review`/`pending_delivery` filters (already built, ADR-026/ADR-032) — no new admin screen needed for the drill-down.
8. **Pending payments count is a direct `payment_status=pending` count** — the same population `app:reconcile-pending-payments` (ADR-021, PAY-3) already targets.
9. **Queue depth is scoped to the `orders` queue only** (`FulfillOrderJob`/`ResendOrderDeliveryJob`/`CheckSupplierDeliveryJob`'s queue), not a breakdown of all four named queues (`default`/`orders`/`price-sync`/`backups`) — `orders` is the one queue whose depth is a genuine delivery-health signal; the others aren't part of the money-critical customer-facing path this screen exists to monitor. Reported as two numbers: pending count (`jobs` table, `queue='orders'`) and failed count (`failed_jobs` table, same queue) — a job that's failed after exhausting retries is a materially different signal from one merely waiting its turn.
10. **`/api/dashboard/health` sits behind `admin.role:super_admin,admin`**, matching `/api/reports/*`'s existing tier (a read-only overview screen, no reason to restrict further than Reports already is).
11. **No caching on the health endpoint — every load computes fresh.** All of DASH-2's data sources are local DB/cache reads (no live supplier network call, per decision 5) — comfortably inside the 2-second budget without a cache layer adding staleness for no real benefit.

### DASH-3 — Conversion Funnel (Orders Created → Payment Confirmed → Delivered, last 7 days)

12. **A real cohort funnel, not three independent daily counts.** Orders *created* in the last 7 days are the cohort; the funnel measures what fraction of that same set reached Payment Confirmed, then Delivered — not three separately-windowed counts (Created by `created_at`, Paid by `paid_at`, Delivered by current status) that would each describe a different set of orders and make "drop-off" meaningless.
13. **Right-censoring is an accepted, documented limitation, not something engineered around.** An order created on day 7 of the window hasn't had time to convert yet and will show as a "drop" even though it may still convert tomorrow. Recorded here rather than silently shipped, same as this project's other accepted-residual calls (e.g. ADR-041's narrower-race-window note) — not worth a corrective mechanism for a 7-day snapshot read.
14. **"Delivered" is read from the order's *current* `delivery_status`, a live snapshot — not a point-in-time-of-delivery check.** This is actually the semantically correct choice for a cohort model (the funnel asks "did this order eventually reach Delivered," not "was it delivered within the 7-day window"), so the fact that `orders` had no `delivered_at` column before this ADR (see decision 21) never blocked DASH-3 itself.
15. **Binary terminal check: only `DeliveryStatus::Delivered` counts as reaching the funnel's last step.** `Failed`/`NeedsReview`/`Pending`/`Processing`/`NotStarted` are all "not yet / dropped," no partial credit.
16. **The Created leg excludes `is_test` orders**, via a new direct `Order::query()` (not `ReportService::scopedOrders()`, which is Paid-only by design) — consistent with every other exclusion of ADR-018 sandbox orders from real metrics.

### DASH-4 — Top Games Weekly Ranking

17. **Reuses `ReportService::gameBreakdown()` unchanged**, called with a rolling trailing-7-day window (today back 6 days, Asia/Kuala_Lumpur) — same window definition as DASH-3, so "weekly" means the same thing everywhere on this screen. Ranking is therefore implicitly Paid-only/`paid_at`-scoped (whatever `scopedOrders()` already enforces), which is correct for a revenue ranking.
18. **"% change" compares the same window against the prior 7-day period** (day 8–14 ago) — two `gameBreakdown()` calls, diffed per game. **"New"** fallback (decision 4's same rule) when a game had zero revenue in the prior window.

### DASH-5 — Hourly Activity

19. **Single-day view, not a 7-day aggregate.** The day selector picks one specific date within the last 7 days; the chart renders that one day's 24 hourly buckets. An aggregate-across-the-week reading would make the day selector meaningless.
20. **Counts orders by `created_at`, excluding `is_test`** — matches DASH-3's Created leg (raw activity/attempt volume, not payment-filtered), giving this screen one consistent "created" definition instead of two.
21. **Hour buckets are 00–23 in Asia/Kuala_Lumpur**, matching every other day/time bucketing already established (`ReportService::dailyTrend()`).

### DASH-6 — Auto-refresh

22. **Only the DASH-2 health section auto-refreshes, every 60 seconds** — DASH-1/3/4/5's figures barely move within an hour; refreshing them on a timer burns backend load for no visible benefit. Plain client-side `setInterval` re-fetch of `/api/dashboard/health` — no WebSocket/SSE/Reverb infrastructure. `laravel/reverb` is not installed anywhere in this codebase, and standing up a broadcast server (new process, a `wss://` port through ADR-020's droplet, TLS for it) is real new infrastructure this project doesn't otherwise need yet, for a 60-second-cadence single-screen number — push-based delivery is the right tool once there's a genuine multi-admin real-time need (e.g. live notifications), not for this.
23. **Always-on, no pause/toggle control.** DASH-6 is an "Important," not MVP, requirement — a pause control is its own small feature not worth building for this.

### Cross-cutting: `orders.delivered_at` and the `definition` convention

24. **New nullable `orders.delivered_at` timestamp column, stamped at the exact point `delivery_status` becomes `Delivered`.** Found while pinning DASH-3 that no such column existed (`paid_at`'s own equivalent was never mirrored for delivery) — the founder's own call once this surfaced: worth fixing now, not scope-creeping around it, since the actual cost turned out low: `OrderStatusService`'s three `Delivered`-returning transitions (`markDelivered()`, `markDeliveredManually()`, `finalizePendingSuccess()`) are all consumed by exactly **three assignment sites, all in one file** (`OrderFulfillmentService.php`) — cheaper than `paid_at`'s own 4-5-file rollout. A backfill migration sets `delivered_at = updated_at` for any already-`Delivered` order missing it, flagged the same way `paid_at`'s own backfill was: `updated_at` is the best available proxy, not a guaranteed-exact original delivery timestamp (an order's `updated_at` could reflect a later, unrelated touch). DASH-3 itself doesn't depend on this column (decision 14) — its value is independent, opening the door to a future delivery-SLA/time-to-deliver metric without another schema pass.
25. **Every KPI/metric value returned by the new `/api/dashboard/*` endpoints ships alongside a `definition` string** — e.g. `{"value": 125000, "definition": "SUM(final_amount) where payment_status=Paid, paid_at = today (Asia/Kuala_Lumpur), excludes is_test orders"}` — rendered as a small clickable `(i)` info affordance on every card, both DASH-1 and DASH-2 through DASH-5 alike. Founder's own reasoning: a future definition change (e.g. deciding "stuck" should mean something different) shouldn't require asking Claude to re-derive and re-explain the current definition first — the answer is already sitting in the API response, self-auditable at any time via the network tab alone. **The definition string is generated backend-side, colocated with the calculation it describes** (in the same `DashboardService`/`ReportService` method, not hand-copied into the frontend) — a definition and its calculation living in two different codebases (Laravel vs. Next.js) would be exactly the kind of two-copies-of-one-fact drift this project's own conventions (ADR-044 decision 6, for instance) already exist to avoid.

### Endpoint shape

26. **Five granular endpoints under a new `Admin\DashboardController`, matching `Admin\ReportController`'s existing one-endpoint-per-concern shape** (lazy-fetched independently by the frontend, same as `/admin/reports`'s per-tab fetch pattern): `GET /api/dashboard/summary` (DASH-1), `GET /api/dashboard/health` (DASH-2, the only one polled per decision 22), `GET /api/dashboard/funnel` (DASH-3), `GET /api/dashboard/top-games` (DASH-4), `GET /api/dashboard/hourly-activity?date=YYYY-MM-DD` (DASH-5, the only one taking a request param, for the day selector). All five share the same `admin.role:super_admin,admin` tier (decision 10).
27. **Business logic lives in a new `App\Services\Dashboard\DashboardService`**, which delegates DASH-1 to `ReportService` (decision 3) rather than duplicating its rules, and owns DASH-2/3/4/5's own logic directly — DASH-3/5 need a raw `Order::query()` (decision 16/20) since `ReportService::scopedOrders()` is Paid-only by design and can't serve a Created-based leg.

**Rationale:** Every metric definition here follows the same discipline Reports established (pin the exact source/timestamp/table before writing a query, not after a bug surfaces) — DASH-3's cohort-vs-three-counts choice and DASH-2's derived-vs-live-ping choice are this ADR's two `Order.platform_profit`-style landmines, both resolved by asking "which one is actually true to what the requirement is asking," not by picking whichever is easiest to query. Reusing `ReportService` (DASH-1/4) and the `delivery_reconciliation` config (DASH-2) instead of parallel re-definitions is a direct application of AGENTS.md's "Single Source of Truth" principle — the same reasoning ADR-044 already applied to zod schemas replacing hand-written interfaces.

**Consequence to track:** The right-censoring bias in DASH-3 (decision 13) means a founder glancing at "today's" funnel drop-off during a traffic spike will see an inflated drop-off rate for orders too recent to have converted yet — worth a one-line UI caveat near the funnel, not just a code comment, so it doesn't get mistaken for a real quality signal. `delivered_at`'s backfill (decision 24) is an approximation for historical rows — don't treat pre-this-migration `delivered_at` values as precise if a future feature (e.g. delivery-SLA reporting) is built on top of it; only rows created after this ADR ships have a trustworthy value. The `definition` string convention (decision 25) is new precedent — any *future* dashboard/report metric this project adds should carry one too, or this screen ends up with some cards self-documenting and others not, undermining the whole point.
